title: fail_fast leaves remaining jobs in Pending state instead of Skipped
description: When fail_fast triggers, BatchProcessor::run returns immediately with BatchReport::from_jobs(jobs, ...). Jobs after the failed one were never iterated, so their status remains JobStatus::Pending. The report's stats.pending will be non-zero and stats.skipped will be 0, contradicting the intent of an aborted batch. ParallelBatch in the same file does mark subsequent chunks as Skipped (line 416-418), so the two code paths are inconsistent.
fix_hint: Before returning from the fail_fast branch, iterate remaining jobs and set status = JobStatus::Skipped.

title: ParallelBatch concurrency limit is silently ignored
description: ParallelBatch::run claims to enforce a concurrency limit but iterates each chunk sequentially with `for job in chunk.iter_mut()`. No threads are spawned. The `concurrency` parameter only controls chunk size, which has no runtime effect on parallelism. A caller setting concurrency=8 expects 8x speed-up; instead jobs run one at a time. The doc comment admits this is a 'stub' but the public API (BatchError::InvalidConcurrency, ParallelBatch::new requiring >=1) implies real parallelism.
fix_hint: Either use std::thread::scope with a semaphore/work-stealing queue, or rename type and document loudly that execution is sequential.

title: expect_value rejects negative numeric option values
description: The peek-ahead in expect_value treats any token starting with '-' (other than the bare '-') as a forgotten value and returns MissingArgument. This wrongly rejects legitimate negative values such as `--config -7` or any future option taking a signed integer / negative offset. The comment justifies catching `--format --quiet`, but the check is too broad: it cannot distinguish a flag from a negative number.
fix_hint: Refine the predicate to only reject tokens that look like flags: longer than one char and starting with '-' followed by a non-digit, e.g. `next.len() > 1 && next.starts_with('-') && !next[1..].starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit())`.

title: Default-config file load silently swallows parse errors
description: When no --config flag is given, Cli::from_argv probes default candidates (`.rustre.cfg`, `rustre.cfg`, `~/.rustre.cfg`). The loop uses `if let Ok(c) = CliConfig::load_from_file(&pb)` and silently falls through on Err. A malformed `.rustre.cfg` in the cwd will be ignored without any diagnostic, then the program runs with the default empty config — the user has no idea their config was rejected. The explicit --config path correctly propagates the error; the default path does not.
fix_hint: At minimum, warn() the user when a candidate exists but fails to parse; or surface the error (only suppress io::ErrorKind::NotFound).

title: Hex literals in config values silently downgraded to String
description: parse_config_value tries i64 then f64 then falls through to String. Common RE values such as `base_addr = 0x400000` will fail i64::from_str (no hex support), fail f64::from_str, and be stored as ConfigValue::String("0x400000"). Callers using get_int() will get None for what looks like an integer. Given the crate's RE focus and that parse_addr() elsewhere accepts 0x-prefixed values, this is a surprising asymmetry.
fix_hint: Before the i64 branch, try parsing hex via the same logic as parse_addr (strip 0x/0X, u64::from_str_radix), then cast or store as Int.

title: parse_short cannot handle combined short option with value
description: parse_short iterates every char of the short token treating each as an independent flag. There is no handling for `-f=json` (would attempt to parse 'f','=','j','s','o','n' as flags and error on '='), nor for `-fjson` (treated as multi-flag). Long form supports `--format=json` via split_once; short form has no equivalent path. Users mixing the two styles will get UnknownCommand('=') which is confusing.
fix_hint: Detect '=' in the short token: if present, split on first '=' and dispatch the leading char as an option-with-value through expect_value or apply_long_kv.

title: fmt_addr falls back to 64-bit width for any non-{16,32} bits value
description: The match arms only handle bits == 16 and bits == 32; every other value (including 8, 24, 48, 0) silently produces a 16-hex-digit padded string. Passing bits=8 for a small embedded MCU address yields 0x0000000000000012 instead of 0x12 — likely surprising. There is no Result/error and no panic for invalid widths.
fix_hint: Either accept only an enum (AddrBits::B16/B32/B64) or panic/Result-error on unexpected bit widths; at minimum document the fallback explicitly.

title: ProgressBar.advance silently caps current to total, hiding overflow
description: `self.current = self.current.saturating_add(n).min(self.total);` silently swallows the case where the caller advances past total. For a long-running RE batch this masks accounting bugs (e.g. double-counting a unit of work) because the bar happily sits at 100% forever and elapsed/ETA become meaningless. There is no debug assertion or warning.
fix_hint: Either debug_assert!(self.current + n <= self.total) or expose an `overshoot` counter so the caller can see when totals were mis-estimated.

title: Table::set_align panics on out-of-bounds column
description: Public API `Table::set_align(col, align)` indexes `self.col_align[col]` directly. A caller passing col >= ncols panics. Documented but still a public-API panic.
fix_hint: Return Result or silently ignore out-of-range indices.

title: PE parser potential usize arithmetic overflow on 32-bit targets
description: `parse_pe_sections_synthetic` reads a 32-bit `e_lfanew` from attacker-controlled bytes and casts to usize, then computes `e_lfanew + 24`, `coff + 20`, `opt_start + opt_header_size`, `sec_table + i * 40`. On a 32-bit target, these additions can wrap around to a small value and then pass the subsequent length check, allowing out-of-bounds slice indexing to panic, or in rarer cases bypass the bounds check. The function is reachable from any caller that feeds untrusted binary data.
fix_hint: Use checked_add throughout and bail on overflow; verify each offset with checked arithmetic against data.len().

title: Mutex held across loop and never poisoned-recovered (low risk)
description: `ParallelBatch::run` uses `Arc<Mutex<bool>>` for an aborted flag and calls `.lock().unwrap()` in two places. If a panicking job leaves the mutex poisoned, the next `lock().unwrap()` will itself panic. Currently the body holding the lock is just a bool write so panics are unlikely, but the unwrap is a latent panic vector. The Mutex is also redundant since the run loop is sequential (no real parallelism).

title: LDD Y+q misdecoded when d>=16
description: The mask `(word & 0x0200) == 0` treats the destination register's MSB as opcode, so any LDD with d>=16 is rejected even though it is a valid encoding.

title: LDD Z+q misdecoded when d>=16
description: Same incorrect `(word & 0x0200) == 0` guard rejects valid LDD Rd,Z+q when the destination register has bit 4 set.

title: BSET/BCLR shadowed by SEC/CLC etc.
description: decode_avr_fixed claims 0x9408..0x94F8 first, so the generic BSET/BCLR arms in decode_avr_alu2 are unreachable, hiding the bit-index operand form.

title: JMP/CALL absolute target multiplied by 2
description: AVR JMP/CALL encodes a word address; `target = ((k_hi<<16)|k_lo) * 2` doubles the byte address, producing wrong targets above 64 KiB.

title: Branch target parsed without bounding to program memory
description: `u64::from_str_radix` accepts any width hex and `get_branches` returns the raw value, so a wrapped negative rel_target (e.g., RJMP -1 at PC=0) yields a bogus ~2^64 branch target.

title: `bytes[..dec.size.min(bytes.len())]` masks truncation
description: If decode_avr returns a 4-byte size but the caller passed only 2 bytes (e.g., end of buffer) the size field still says 4 while raw is 2 — downstream code that trusts `instr.size` advances past EOF.

title: Backward-jump loop detector misses self-loop
description: `target < i` excludes a jump-to-self (target == i), so infinite self-loops are not flagged as loops/unbounded.

title: Bounds check casts negative base/offset to u64
description: `offset as u64` and `base as u64 + len` wrap negative i64 to enormous u64, making `check_bounds` return Safe for cases that should be Unsafe when base/offset are negative but not strictly less than each other.

title: Jump target cast from i64 to usize without negative check
description: `(pc as i64 + 1 + insn.off as i64) as usize` wraps to huge usize on negative result; subsequent `< program.len()` check still treats it as out-of-bounds error rather than ignoring, but a backward jump (off negative making target valid) is silently treated as forward visit and may not enqueue the real backward target — back-edges to PC 0 work only by coincidence.

title: Field reloc ignores access string and always uses members[0]
description: `apply` for FieldByteOffset/FieldByteSize patches the immediate with the FIRST member regardless of the parsed access indices, silently producing wrong offsets for any field other than the first.

title: Fat section data_size u24 decoded with wrong byte placement
description: Using `from_le_bytes([0, bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])` shifts each byte up by 8 bits, producing a value 256x too large and an inflated clause count.

title: Stream header loop indexes `data[off..]` without bounds check
description: If `off` exceeds `data.len()` after a previous iteration, slicing panics instead of returning an error.

title: stream_data computes `start + size` without checked_add
description: On 32-bit or with huge attacker-controlled size, addition wraps and `.get()` may return a non-empty unintended slice.

title: `16 + version_len` may overflow usize on 32-bit when version_len is attacker-controlled u32
description: Untrusted u32 added to 16 without checked_add can wrap to small value, bypassing subsequent length check.

title: Small-format data_size read as single u8 but spec is u8
description: Per ECMA-335 the small section data_size IS u8 so max 255 bytes — fine, but no validation that data_size >= 4 before subtraction (saturating_sub hides malformed input as zero clauses, silently).

title: `raw: data.to_vec()` clones entire input buffer on every parse
description: Unnecessary heap allocation/copy; should borrow or accept ownership explicitly.

title: Fat EH section data_size u24 decoded with wrong byte placement
description: `u32::from_le_bytes([0, bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]])` left-shifts each byte by an extra 8 bits, yielding a value 256x too large and an inflated clause_count.

title: stream_data uses unchecked start + size for slice end
description: Attacker-controlled u32 offset+size can wrap on 32-bit targets, and there is no validation that end >= start before .get(start..end).

title: version_end = 16 + version_len uses untrusted u32 without checked_add
description: A crafted version_len near usize::MAX wraps to a small index, defeating the subsequent length check and yielding wrong parse results.

title: Small-format clause_count uses saturating_sub on data_size
description: Malformed sections with data_size < 4 are silently treated as zero clauses rather than reported as Truncated, hiding parser errors from callers.

title: CilMetadataReader::parse clones the entire input buffer into self.raw
description: Unnecessary heap copy on every parse; should borrow with a lifetime or accept Vec<u8> ownership.

title: tableswitch high-low+1 can overflow i32
description: `(high - low + 1)` is computed in i32 on attacker-controlled values and will panic in debug / wrap in release before the `.max(0)` saturates it.

title: tableswitch count arithmetic overflows i32
description: Same `(high - low + 1)` pattern; `high=i32::MAX, low<0` overflows before clamp, and `count * 4` can also overflow usize on 32-bit hosts leading to undersized `need` check.

title: get_branches mis-reads goto_w/jsr_w/switch targets
description: All branch/call instrs are decoded as i16 from bytes[1..3], but goto_w/jsr_w carry a 4-byte offset and tableswitch/lookupswitch have no such field — branch target is wrong.

title: lookupswitch npairs*8 can overflow usize
description: `npairs * 8` is unchecked; a malicious i32 npairs near i32::MAX produces a usize overflow on 32-bit and a `need` check that never trips on 64-bit allows huge allocations.

title: make_iabc silently truncates out-of-range operands
description: Fields a/b/c/k are masked-into-position with raw shifts (e.g. `c << 24`) without range checks, so values >=256 corrupt adjacent instruction fields instead of erroring.

title: Legacy field layout comment contradicts implementation
description: Top-of-file comment claims B is at bits 14..22 and C at 23..31, but get_b_old reads `w>>23` and get_c_old reads `w>>14`, so either the docs or the extractors are wrong for Lua 5.1–5.3 (B and C may be swapped).

title: Branch target multiplication can panic in debug
description: `off as u64 * 4` is a checked multiplication; a malformed disassembly token with a large negative offset becomes a huge u64 and overflows on `*4`, panicking in debug builds.

title: make_iasbx has no sBx range validation
description: `(sbx + MAXARG_SBX) as u32` will panic on overflow in debug or silently wrap in release when callers pass an out-of-range sBx, producing a malformed instruction word.

title: Jump target cast to usize hides negative targets
description: `(i as i64 + 1 + sj as i64) as usize` silently produces a giant usize for negative resolved targets, so jump_targets() returns bogus indices instead of filtering invalid jumps.

title: make_shri/make_shli silently mis-encode out-of-range C
description: `(c + 127) as u32 & 0xff` quietly wraps for c<-127 or c>128 instead of returning an error, producing wrong shift amounts in the emitted instruction.

title: num_bc * 4 multiplication can overflow usize
description: num_bc is an attacker-controlled ULEB128 length used unchecked in `num_bc * 4` and `p + bc_bytes`, allowing wraparound that bypasses the bounds check on 32-bit targets and yields out-of-bounds reads.

title: KGC string ktype==5 case is dead and drops zero-length strings
description: The explicit `5 =>` arm matches before the `n if n >= 5` arm but only pushes `LjConst::Nil`, so empty strings (len=0) are silently lost instead of being parsed as `String(vec![])`.

title: Jump offset truncated to u16 without range check
description: `(offset + 0x8000) as u16` silently wraps when the label distance exceeds the signed-16-bit window, producing a wrong jump target instead of an error.

title: Addition `p + bc_bytes` may wrap
description: After the multiplication wrap above, `p + bc_bytes` is also not a checked_add, so on overflow the comparison `p + bc_bytes > proto_data.len()` is false and the loop reads past the buffer.

title: `LJ_NAMES.get(op as usize).copied().unwrap_or` is fine but surrounding `decode(...).unwrap()` in tests/lib paths can panic
description: Decoder `unwrap()` calls in the compat layer (lines 447,457,516,524,551) would panic on malformed input if reused outside tests.

title: LE decode of MIPS instruction words
description: MIPS code (especially N64/console) is overwhelmingly big-endian yet `MipsFunctionProfiler::profile` uses `u32::from_le_bytes`, mis-decoding every instruction on BE targets.

title: DelaySlotAnalyzer assumes little-endian
description: `DelaySlotAnalyzer::scan` (and GlobalPointerUsage/MipsTlb/MipsBranchTargetTable/scan_for_eret) decode words via `from_le_bytes`, so all detection silently fails on big-endian MIPS images.

title: FCC shift can overflow
description: `set_fcc`/`get_fcc` compute `24 + cc as u32` with no bounds check on `cc`; cc>=8 (or even cc>7 via decoded field) yields shift >=31 and `1 << shift` overflow panic in debug builds.

title: CVT.W produces float, not integer bits
description: `CvtWS/CvtWD` cast to `i32` then store via `set_single/set_double`, re-converting to float; MIPS CVT.W.fmt must store the integer bit pattern (use `f32::from_bits(i as u32)` semantics), so downstream MFC1 reads the wrong value.

title: branch_target signed overflow on kernel PCs
description: `(pc as i32 + 4 + offset) as u32` overflows in debug when pc>=0x8000_0000 (kseg0/kseg1 — the typical region for MIPS code), causing panic.

title: Wrong stack slot growth for O32 overflow args
description: `self.stack_offset += size.max(self.stack_align)` bumps offset by 8 for a 4-byte O32 arg, mismodeling O32's 4-byte argument slots and producing wrong stack offsets for subsequent args.

title: IndirectAutoInc on PC with byte mode increments by 1
description: MSP430 spec mandates PC autoincrement is always 2 (even byte ops), so #imm byte fetches corrupt PC alignment.

title: Invalid Op1 opcode silently decoded as RETI
description: `Op1::from_bits(opcode3).unwrap_or(Op1::Reti)` mis-decodes opcodes 7 as RETI instead of returning Data/error.

title: write_operand silently drops writes for Indexed/Indirect single-op destinations
description: RRC/RRA/SWPB/SXT with memory operand discard the result, corrupting emulation semantics.

title: DADD implemented as binary ADDC instead of BCD
description: Produces wrong results for any BCD code and silently passes flags through.

title: Missing-extension-word truncation masked by unwrap_or(0)
description: `ext(...)` returning None is silently treated as 0, producing fabricated operands instead of an InvalidFormat error.

title: Absolute branch target not sign-extended on 64-bit
description: branch_target with aa=1 zero-extends negative offset via u32 cast, producing wrong 64-bit absolute target for ppc64.

title: xo=536 wrongly decoded as SRW
description: Extended opcode 536 is SRD (shift right doubleword), not an alias of SRW (xo=26), causing wrong mnemonic on 64-bit code.

title: xo=27 misdecoded as MULHW
description: Only xo=75 is MULHW; xo=27 is reserved and should not alias MULHW.

title: xo=18 misdecoded as RFI
description: Extended opcode 18 is reserved (or RFID on 64-bit), not RFI; aliasing it to RFI yields wrong analysis.

title: BC AA bit ignored in mnemonic
description: Opcode 16 decoder never emits the "A" suffix for absolute conditional branches (BCA/BCLA), so absolute conditional branches are misnamed.

title: BCLR always flagged RET regardless of condition/LK
description: Conditional bclr and bclrl (call-through-LR) are unconditionally tagged InstrFlags::RET, breaking CFG and call analysis.

title: c_swsp_imm reads wrong bit fields
description: `(hw >> 9) & 3` and `(hw >> 7) & 0xF` extract bits [10:9]/[10:7] but C.SWSP imm requires inst[8:7] and inst[12:9], producing wrong store offsets.

title: c_sdsp_imm swaps high/low immediate fields
description: b8b6 takes hw>>10 (inst[12:10]) and b5b3 takes hw>>7 (inst[9:7]); shifts are inverted vs the spec (inst[9:7]=imm[8:6], inst[12:10]=imm[5:3]).

title: c_lw_imm extracts wrong bits
description: reads `(hw>>2)&7` and `(hw>>10)&7` but C.LW spec needs inst[5]=off[6], inst[12:10]=off[5:3], inst[6]=off[2]; produces incorrect load offsets.

title: c.fld decode uses doubled +8 and wrong rs1 field
description: `xr(rs2_prime + 8)` adds 8 to an already-+8 prime register and uses bits [2:4] (rd' field) instead of rs1' bits [9:7], yielding wrong base register.

title: C.LW/C.SW immediate uses (raw>>10)&3 (2 bits) instead of 3
description: spec encodes imm[5:3] in inst[12:10] (3 bits); masking with 3 drops bit 12, producing wrong offsets.

title: decode_word_full panics on raw.len()<4
description: public `decode_word_full` slices `raw[..4]` without a length check, so callers can trigger a panic from untrusted input.

title: SLL/SRL/SRA use wrong op3 encodings
description: emulator matches op3 0x0D/0x0E/0x0F for SLL/SRL/SRA, but SPARC V8 spec assigns 0x25/0x26/0x27 (decoder agrees), so shifts never execute and reserved encodings fire instead.

title: Bicc condition table swapped between LE and LEU
description: eval_bicc returns C|Z for cond=0x2 (which is BLE per Cond enum, expected Z|(N^V)) and n for 0x4 (which is BLEU, expected C|Z), so branch evaluations are systematically wrong.

title: Bicc annul/condition bits decoded from wrong field positions
description: annul is bit 29 (top of rd field, `rd>>4`) and cond is bits[28:25] (`rd & 0xF`), but code uses `rd>>1` for cond and `rd & 1` for annul, mis-decoding every Bicc/FBfcc.

title: exec_call signed shift overflow
description: `((instr & 0x3FFF_FFFF) as i32) << 2` shifts a positive i32 up to 0x3FFFFFFF left by 2, overflowing into the sign bit and panicking in debug builds for any CALL with disp30 bit 29 set.

title: read_u32/write_u32 use non-wrapping add on u32 addresses
description: `addr + 1/2/3` panics on debug builds when addr is near u32::MAX instead of wrapping or reporting a data fault.

title: VEX/EVEX tail decode treats opcode byte as ModRM
description: After advancing past the VEX/EVEX payload, pos still points at the opcode byte (not past it), so modrm_and_imm reads the opcode as a ModRM and computes a length one byte short with wrong displacements.

title: 3-byte VEX (C4) length misses opcode byte
description: pos += 3 only consumes C4 + 2 payload bytes, leaving the opcode unconsumed before decode_vex_tail uses bytes[pos] as ModRM.

title: EVEX length misses opcode byte
description: pos += 4 covers 62h + 3 payload bytes but not the opcode, so the subsequent ModRM read is off by one for every EVEX instruction.

title: Unary negation panics on i32::MIN displacement
description: `(-disp) as u32` overflows in debug builds when disp == i32::MIN; use wrapping_neg() or i64 widening.

title: Same i32::MIN negation panic in BasePlusIndex display
description: Identical `-disp` overflow path for the indexed addressing form.

title: Same i32::MIN negation panic in RipRelative display
description: `(-disp) as u32` on i32::MIN traps in debug; rip-relative displacements can legitimately reach the minimum value.

title: NEG PV flag overwritten by parity
description: set_pv(self.a==0x80) sets overflow but the subsequent update_szpv_byte recomputes PV from parity, destroying overflow indication.

title: R register single-increment for prefixed ops
description: Real Z80 increments R twice for CB/DD/ED/FD-prefixed instructions; emulator increments once, so code reading R for self-modification/checksums will diverge.

title: execute_index fallback recurses on prefix bytes
description: When op2 is itself CB/DD/ED/FD, calling execute(op2,...) re-fetches subsequent bytes as the new prefix payload, producing nonsense decode/exec.

title: set_s uses redundant `v & true` mask
description: `v & true` is just v; harmless but indicates copy-paste error suggesting intent to mask another value, leaving a latent maintenance bug.

title: DAA always clears H flag
description: Z80 DAA should set H based on bit-4 transition during BCD correction, not unconditionally clear it.

title: Z80Memory::load silently truncates and may overflow usize
description: `start + bytes.len()` can overflow usize on 32-bit when bytes.len() is huge; oversize loads are silently truncated with no error returned.

title: Single quote char panics in parse_value
description: A 1-char string like `"` satisfies both starts_with and ends_with, and slicing `s[1..s.len()-1]` becomes `s[1..0]` which panics.

title: ELF machine read as fixed little-endian
description: EI_DATA (byte 5) is ignored so big-endian ELFs (MIPS/PPC) report wrong machine type.

title: Mach-O 32-bit magic mislabeled bits/arch
description: FEEDFACE branch sets arch="x86_64" but bits=32, an inconsistent classification.

title: u64 length cast to usize
description: `len as usize` truncates the user-supplied --length on 32-bit targets, silently shrinking the scan window.

title: Disasm address addition can overflow
description: `self.args.start + i as u64 * 4` is unchecked and wraps when start is near u64::MAX.

title: ELF bits detection ignores invalid EI_CLASS
description: Treats anything other than 2 as 32-bit, so a corrupt/0 EI_CLASS is silently reported as 32-bit.

title: Single quote char panics in parse_value
description: A 1-char string like `"` satisfies both starts_with and ends_with checks and the slice s[1..s.len()-1] becomes s[1..0] which panics.

title: ELF e_machine always read little-endian
description: EI_DATA byte is ignored so big-endian ELFs (MIPS/PPC/SPARC) decode the machine field with wrong byte order.

title: Mach-O 32-bit magic mislabels arch
description: The FEEDFACE branch sets arch="x86_64" while bits=32, producing an inconsistent file-info record.

title: u64 length cast to usize
description: `len as usize` truncates the user-supplied --length value on 32-bit targets, silently shrinking the scan window.

title: Disasm address arithmetic can overflow
description: `self.args.start + i as u64 * 4` is unchecked and wraps around when start is near u64::MAX.

title: ELF bits detection accepts any non-2 as 32-bit
description: A corrupt or zero EI_CLASS byte is silently reported as 32-bit instead of being flagged unknown.

title: Tilde in default config path not expanded
description: The literal "~/.rustre.cfg" candidate is passed to PathBuf without home expansion, so the user's home config is never loaded.

title: terminal_supports_color disables color on Windows by default
description: Returning false when TERM is Err treats normal Windows consoles (where TERM is unset) as non-color terminals.

title: fail_fast does not abort remaining jobs within current chunk
description: Setting *aborted=true only skips the next chunk; the inner `for job in chunk` keeps running, so fail_fast can execute many extra jobs.

title: Progress bar width subtraction can underflow
description: `self.width - filled` panics if floating-point rounding makes `filled > width` (e.g. width near usize::MAX, or future code paths bypassing the saturating cap on current).

title: String values like "inf"/"nan"/"1e5" silently parsed as Float
description: parse_value tries f64 before string fallback, so user-intended strings such as "inf" become Float(infinity), corrupting config semantics.

title: `Sub<Address> for Address` silently saturates on underflow
description: Using `a - b` where `b > a` returns 0 instead of panicking or signaling, hiding wrong offset bugs in callers that assume normal subtraction semantics.

title: `Memory::read` returns SegmentFault for in-range addresses past data length
description: If `offset_in_seg >= seg.data.len()` (valid range but short data, like BSS), the loop never advances and returns SegmentFault even though the address is mapped.

title: `has_magic_at` computes `offset + needle.len()` unchecked
description: Addition can overflow usize when offset is large, panicking in debug builds; should use `offset.checked_add(needle.len())`.

title: EndianRead for [u8] computes `offset + N` without checked add
description: `self.get(offset..offset + 2)` (and the u32/u64/u128 variants) will panic in debug when offset is near `usize::MAX`; should use `offset.checked_add(N)`.

title: `Patch::read_patched` zero-fills non-overlap bytes inside the requested window
description: For requested ranges that extend past the patch, the result contains 0x00 for the non-patched portion instead of the underlying binary bytes, silently corrupting reads that span patch boundaries.

title: `BinaryUri::parse` performs no validation or normalization of scheme/path
description: Untrusted URIs are split on `://` and stored verbatim, allowing path-traversal sequences and arbitrary schemes to flow downstream to loaders unchecked.

title: MemoryRegion::contains can overflow
description: base + size is unchecked u64 addition; a region near u64::MAX wraps and contains() returns wrong results.

title: MemoryInspector::read addr+size unchecked
description: addr + size as u64 and base + data.len() as u64 can wrap silently, allowing a read past mapped end to spuriously succeed or fail.

title: read_u64_le unwraps try_into
description: If read returns fewer than 8 bytes (shouldn't, but no invariant enforced), try_into().unwrap() panics in library code.

title: MockDebugger::read_memory silently truncates
description: end = (offset+size).min(page.len()) returns fewer bytes than requested with no error, breaking the read_memory contract.

title: MockDebugger::write_memory is a no-op that reports success
description: Ignores addr/data entirely and returns Ok(data.len()), producing false-positive writes that mask test bugs.

title: DebugEvent timestamp truncates u128 nanos to u64
description: d.as_nanos() as u64 silently truncates; safe until ~2554 but the `as` cast hides overflow and there's no #[allow] or comment.

title: Binary memory write payload corrupted by UTF-8 lossy conversion
description: `write_binary_cmd` runs escaped raw bytes through `String::from_utf8_lossy`, replacing any non-UTF8 byte (most bytes >0x7F) with U+FFFD, so the `X` packet transmits wrong data to the target.

title: is_connected defaults to true on lock contention
description: `try_lock().map(...).unwrap_or(true)` reports a disconnected/contended debugger as connected, leading callers to issue commands that will fail.

title: step_over PC+5 can wrap u64
description: `pc + 5` on a u64 PC near address-space end overflows in debug builds (panic) and wraps silently in release, planting a breakpoint at address 0.

title: Backtrace fp+16 can wrap u64
description: `sp = fp + 16` during frame-pointer unwind has no checked_add; a corrupt or attacker-controlled saved rbp causes panic/wrap.

title: memory-map qXfer length capped at 0xfff bytes
description: Requesting only 4095 bytes of the memory-map XML silently truncates the map for any non-trivial target, returning a partial/empty `Vec<MemoryMap>`.

title: All-0xFF register chunk misidentified as "unavailable"
description: Real registers with legitimate value 0xFFFF... (e.g. -1 sentinels, MXCSR masks) are dropped from the RegisterSet because the unavailable marker is `xx` (not 0xff bytes) per GDB spec.

title: return_status overlaps processor field
description: return_status is parsed from bytes [4..8] which reuses bytes 4-5 already used for `processor`, instead of bytes [4..8] non-overlapping (should likely be data[8..12] or padding); wrong field decoding.

title: from_bytes panics on truncated packet
description: `raw[HEADER_SIZE..HEADER_SIZE + byte_count]` slices without verifying raw.len() >= that range, causing a panic on a short/malformed packet from an attacker-controlled transport.

title: byte_count truncates data.len() to u16
description: `data.len() as u16` silently wraps when payload exceeds 65535 bytes, producing a malformed packet with mismatched length.

title: parse_recv re-parses already-consumed bytes after short packet
description: when from_bytes succeeds but recv_buf has fewer than `total` bytes the loop breaks without consuming, yet next iteration re-decodes the same header repeatedly; also `from_bytes` returns Some even when payload bytes are missing (out-of-bounds risk via line 250 panic).

title: O(n) remove(0) on malformed stream
description: on unknown packet type, `recv_buf.remove(0)` is O(n); a stream of garbage bytes causes quadratic CPU usage.

title: Unchecked address+size in map overlap check
description: `address + size` and `r.address + r.size` can wrap u64 and bypass overlap detection, allowing aliased regions.

title: Unbounded allocation from caller-controlled size
description: `vec![0u8; size as usize]` panics or OOMs when callers pass huge sizes, and `size as usize` truncates on 32-bit hosts.

title: read() silently zero-pads past region end
description: Reading more than region size returns zero-padded buffer instead of an error, masking out-of-bounds reads.

title: VmRegionInfo::end() overflows on high addresses
description: `self.address + self.size` is unchecked u64 addition; a region near u64::MAX overflows and makes `contains` wrongly return false.

title: cpsr truncated via `as u32` without check
description: `Arm64ThreadState::from_array` silently drops the upper 32 bits of element 33 when constructing cpsr.

title: page_align overflows on large values
description: value + page_size-1 wraps to 0 for inputs near u64::MAX, producing wrong alignment.

title: add_section size arithmetic can underflow/overflow
description: section.address - addr + section.size has no checked arithmetic and panics or wraps on crafted inputs.

title: read_memory bounds check overflows
description: addr + size as u64 can wrap past u64::MAX, bypassing the end check and slicing out-of-bounds (panic).

title: map_memory allows overlapping regions silently
description: memory.insert overwrites prior mappings sharing a base and never validates overlap between distinct bases, corrupting reads/writes.

title: MappedRegion::contains overflows on large base
description: self.base + self.data.len() as u64 can wrap, making contains() return wrong results for high addresses.

title: run() increments pc without checking overflow
description: self.pc += 1 panics in debug / wraps in release when pc reaches u64::MAX during long runs.

title: launch command line concatenation lacks arg quoting
description: Args are appended with a plain space so values containing spaces or quotes are mis-parsed by CreateProcessW and enable argument injection.

title: access-violation write flag hardcoded to false
description: decode_exception always reports is_write:false instead of reading ExceptionInformation[0] which encodes read/write/DEP, giving callers wrong fault classification.

title: PAGE_GUARD regions reported as readable
description: eff_protect strips PAGE_GUARD before the match, so guard pages are marked readable/writable even though touching them raises STATUS_GUARD_PAGE_VIOLATION.

title: read_process_memory allocates attacker-controlled size with no cap
description: vec![0u8; size] honours an unchecked usize from the caller; a bogus size triggers multi-GB allocation or OOM abort.

title: process/module enumeration silently truncates at 1024 entries
description: EnumProcesses/EnumProcessModules are called with a fixed buffer and no retry-with-larger-buffer when bytes_needed equals the buffer size, so large systems lose entries.

title: decode_unload_dll discards the actual DLL path
description: The function ignores its lookup and synthesises "dll@{base:#x}" as the path, so LibraryUnload events never carry the real module name even when it is known.

title: Unescaped string literal in CExpr Display
description: StrLit emits `"{s}"` without escaping quotes/backslashes, producing invalid or injectable C output.

title: Negative offset cast i64 to u32 truncates
description: `(-offset) as u32` silently truncates large negative stack offsets, producing colliding variable names.

title: frame_size negates i64 to u64 unchecked
description: `(-o) as u64` on i64::MIN wraps to 0, hiding huge frames; on any positive-after-negation value it's fine but no overflow guard.

title: Recursive convert_block has no depth bound
description: Deep/large CFGs cause unbounded recursion and stack overflow in lib code.

title: Recursive dfs_post on CFG
description: post_order recurses per successor with no iterative fallback; large CFGs overflow the stack.

title: Switch cases labeled by successor index, not real case value
description: Generated switch uses positional index `i` as case label, producing semantically wrong C for any non-trivial jump table.

title: UIntLit u64 cast to i64 corrupts constant folding
description: `*n as i64` wraps u64 values >i64::MAX to negative, producing wrong folded results for unsigned arithmetic.

title: Signed div/mod applied to unsigned constants
description: fold_int_op uses signed `/` and `%` on i64 values that may originate from unsigned literals, giving wrong quotient/remainder for large operands.

title: Dead-assignment elimination drops initializers with side effects
description: Removing `Decl { init: Some(call_with_side_effects) }` when the var is unread silently discards the call, changing program behavior.

title: fold_int_op accepts shift amount >= 64 producing wrong result
description: `wrapping_shl(r as u32)` masks shift mod 32/64 silently and casts negative-rejected r but doesn't reject r>=bitwidth, folding to a value C would treat as UB.

title: IntLit unconditionally typed as int32 makes (long)42 look redundant
description: `infer_type` returns Int(32,true) for any IntLit so casts of integer literals to wider/narrower types are wrongly removed as redundant.

title: Byte indexing with `as char` misclassifies multibyte chars as ident chars
description: `text.as_bytes()[abs-1] as char` treats a UTF-8 continuation byte as a Latin-1 char, so word-boundary detection is incorrect near non-ASCII text.

title: JumpTable::validate ignores function range
description: The `fstart`/`fend` are bound but never compared against `self.targets`, so out-of-function targets pass validation; also `mem` parameter unused.

title: Unchecked address arithmetic in jump table read
description: `base_addr + (i * entry_size) as u64` can wrap on large `i*entry_size` or near u64::MAX, producing wrong entry addresses with no bounds check.

title: Trip count cast loses precision and may panic
description: `(range as f64 / stride.abs() as f64).ceil() as u64` truncates negatives silently and `stride.abs()` panics on `i64::MIN`; also `limit - init` can overflow.

title: AtMost trip count uses wrong formula
description: `limit.unsigned_abs() / stride.unsigned_abs()` ignores sign and that no `init` was provided, giving nonsensical upper bounds for negative limits.

title: Recursive DFS for back-edges can blow stack
description: `dfs_back_edges` (and `dfs_post`) recurses per CFG edge; large functions (deep CFGs) will overflow the stack â€” should be iterative.

title: is_safe_to_inline allows inlining side-effecting expr at single use
description: Returns true for any single-use def regardless of side effects, letting Loads/Calls be reordered across other side-effecting code and changing program semantics.

title: size*8 overflows u8 for large loads
description: `size * 8` is u8 arithmetic; sizes >= 32 panic in debug and wrap silently in release, producing wrong C cast widths.

title: ExprRewriter does not recurse into Call/Load/Ternary/Index/FieldAccess children
description: `rewrite` only descends into BinOp/UnOp, so rules silently never fire on subexpressions inside calls, loads, ternaries, etc.

title: Width information lost in simplifier identity rules
description: Rules like `a-a`, `x*0`, `x%1` return `Const(_, I64)` regardless of operand width, corrupting later type-aware passes.

title: print_const renders negative signed constants as 64-bit hex
description: For negative i64 with I8/I16/I32 width, falls to `0x{v:X}` formatting which prints sign-extended huge hex (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF for -1) instead of `-1`.

title: count_shared ignores Call/Load/Ternary/Index nodes
description: Similarity heuristic returns 0 for identical-structured calls, ternaries, loads, etc., greatly underestimating similarity outside BinOp/UnOp subtrees.

title: Empty pool acquire panics
description: `acquire()` on a zero-sized pool indexes `clients[0]` (max(1) doesn't grow the Vec) causing index-out-of-bounds panic.

title: IntCarryLow/High mnemonics not parseable
description: `mnemonic()` emits `INT_CARRY_LOW`/`HIGH` but `from_mnemonic` has no case, so serialized ops can never be deserialized back.

title: Dominator computation uses min(addr) merge
description: Cooper-style dominator iteration replaced with `pa.min(aa)` over raw block IDs, producing semantically wrong immediate dominators.

title: PcodeBlock end set to addr+1
description: `push` sets `end = instr.machine_addr + 1` ignoring instruction length and can move `end` backwards when pushing out-of-order instructions.

title: Stack offset cast u64 as i64
description: `vn.offset as i64` reinterprets large unsigned offsets as huge negative numbers, producing wrong stack slot display for offsets >= 2^63.

title: Left shift can panic/overflow on attacker-controlled scale
description: `1u64 << shift` where `shift` is `i64 as u64` panics in debug and wraps in release when `shift >= 64`, and large/negative shifts can come from any input expression.

title: Negative multiplier cast to huge u64 scale
description: `scale as u64` on a negative `i64` constant produces a huge positive scale, then compared with `expected_size`, leading to incorrect array-index recognition and possible later overflow.

title: Unchecked `inner.byte_size()? * n` for arrays
description: `Array(inner, n).byte_size()` multiplies element size by count with no `checked_mul`, silently wrapping for large N and producing wrong layout sizes.

title: `field_at` matches zero-size field at any offset >= its start
description: The branch `field_end == f.offset` (zero-size or unknown-size field) makes the predicate true for every `offset >= f.offset`, so any unknown-size field swallows all later offsets.

title: `TypeUnifier::find` uses unbounded recursion
description: Path compression is implemented with recursive `find` calls; a long parent chain (easy to construct from `add_constraint`) overflows the stack instead of resolving.

title: byte-to-char cast corrupts non-ASCII
description: `self.input.get(pos).map(|&b| b as char)` reinterprets each UTF-8 byte as a Latin-1 char, corrupting multi-byte identifiers and producing wrong `name` strings.

title: base-36 substitution accepts lowercase
description: substitution index parser accepts `is_ascii_alphanumeric` (lowercase) for `S<id>_` though Itanium ABI only permits uppercase, leading to mis-resolved substitutions.

title: backref cap silently drops names
description: name backrefs hard-capped at 10 means deeper qualified names will fail to resolve subsequent `0-9` digit backrefs even when valid.

title: unchecked i + len in swift heuristic
description: `i + len > bytes.len()` can wrap on overflow when len is huge, bypassing the bound and causing a panic at the subsequent slice.

title: name.push of byte-as-char yields mojibake
description: parse_msvc_qualified_name builds identifier strings via `p.next()? as char`, corrupting non-ASCII bytes instead of decoding UTF-8.

title: S<id>_ accepts lowercase base-36 digits
description: Itanium spec only allows uppercase A-Z for substitution indices; accepting lowercase via is_ascii_alphanumeric makes wrong substitutions resolve silently.

title: substitution idx + 1 can wrap
description: `unwrap_or(0) + 1` will panic in debug if idx_str parses to usize::MAX and silently wrap in release.

title: name_backrefs capped at 10 drops valid entries
description: hard cap means later digit backrefs reference stale or wrong components in long qualified names, producing wrong demangled output.

title: Base64 decode skips final quartet
description: `while i + 3 < input.len()` should be `i + 4 <= input.len()` â€” for a 4-char input the loop never executes, so every input whose length is exactly a multiple of 4 loses its last group.

title: Patch::apply may panic when original longer than patched
description: the bounds check uses `patched.len()` for `end` but the original-comparison slice `data[self.offset..self.offset + self.original.len()]` is indexed without a separate length check, causing an out-of-bounds panic when `original.len() > patched.len()`.

title: Section entropy truncated via `as u32` cast
description: `(entropy * 100.0) as u32` silently truncates negative/NaN floats to 0 and loses precision, breaking `looks_packed` thresholds.

title: elapsed_ms cast u128 to u64
description: `start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64` truncates silently for runs longer than ~584 million years but more practically loses the wider type's safety net.

title: Passes that change length are silently dropped
description: The `if result.len() == current.len()` guard discards any pass whose output differs in length, never applying real deobfuscation that adds/removes bytes.

title: Perturbation resets no_progress before retrying
description: Setting `no_progress_count = 0` immediately after perturbing means the loop cannot detect that perturbation also failed and will keep perturbing forever in pathological cases.

title: partial_cmp().unwrap() panics on NaN quality_delta
description: `rank_perturbations` will panic if any `quality_delta` is NaN (e.g. from log2(0) edge cases in entropy), use `total_cmp` instead.

title: Hash-constant heuristic ignores endianness
description: `u32::from_le_bytes` is hardcoded to little-endian; big-endian binaries will have their hash constants completely missed by the IADL detector.

title: partial_cmp unwrap panics on NaN scores
description: select_best uses partial_cmp(..).unwrap() which panics if any combined_score is NaN, and the same pattern recurs at line 1943.

title: Negative jump target cast to usize wraps
description: `(end as i64 + 2 + i64::from(rel)) as usize` for a negative backward branch produces a huge usize with no bounds validation before returning as a CFG successor (also at line 706).

title: step_by(0) panics when window_size is 1
description: `step_by(self.window_size / 2)` panics when window_size==1 since step_by requires non-zero step, and the constructor does not validate window_size.

title: offset+length addition may overflow usize
description: `planned.offset + planned.length` is computed before the bounds check, so a malicious/garbage plan triggers a debug-mode overflow panic; should use saturating_add like the PatchApplicator does.

title: enumerate_values has no combinatorial cap
description: Doc claims sample_count cap but function unconditionally generates range^n entries causing OOM/DoS for >=3 variables at default bits=8 (16M+ HashMaps).

title: Signed test domain never reaches negative values
description: Comment promises sign-extension but `indices[i] as i64` of a small u64 yields only non-negative values, so opaque predicates relying on negative inputs (e.g. signed comparisons) are misclassified.

title: bits.min(16) silently truncates configured width
description: TruthTableChecker.bits is u32 but enumeration silently caps at 16 with no error/warning, so callers configuring 32-bit domains test a tiny subset and may report AlwaysTrue for predicates false at larger values.

title: Shl/Shr accepts u8 shift but wrapping_shl masks to 6 bits
description: OpaqueExpr::Shl(_, n: u8) allows n>=64, then wrapping_shl(n as u32) silently masks the shift count, diverging from real machine semantics and causing wrong classification of shift-based predicates.

title: classify returns Unknown when all assignments evaluate to None
description: After the loop, `(false,false)` (all div-by-zero) returns Unknown but earlier in-loop early-return on None makes this dead; also if vars empty and is_const None, returns Unknown — inconsistent with Unknown vs unevaluable semantics.

title: wrapping_abs of i64::MIN yields i64::MIN
description: Abs evaluator uses wrapping_abs so Abs(i64::MIN)==i64::MIN, breaking the abs(x)>=0 invariant (Pattern 21) when that input appears, producing incorrect AlwaysTrue classification.

title: XOR-loop region size derived from wrong byte
description: `end = dest_addr + u64::from(key)` where `key = data[i+1]` is the low byte of the imm32 counter, not the loop count, producing incorrect region lengths.

title: Rol/Ror algorithm dispatch swapped
description: `SmcAlgorithm::Rol` invokes `ror8` and `SmcAlgorithm::Ror` invokes `rol8`, contradicting the documented semantics on lines 46-49.

title: extract_key_from_block mask is wrong
description: `block[i+1] & 0x30 == 0x30` matches many non-XOR ModR/M bytes; the XOR opcode-extension nibble check should use `& 0x38 == 0x30` like `trace()` does.

title: ADD-loop opcode mask too loose
description: `data[i+1] & 0xF8 == 0x00` matches ModR/M bytes 0x00-0x07 used by many `80 /reg` forms (including XOR, OR), causing false ADD detections.

title: Negative jump cast wraps to huge usize
description: `(pc as i64 + 2 + offset) as usize` with a negative result wraps to ~`usize::MAX`, relying on the loop condition rather than a safe checked conversion.

title: reconstruct() can overflow base_addr+i
description: `base_addr + i as u64` is unchecked; a near-`u64::MAX` `base_addr` plus index wraps silently and produces wrong map lookups.

title: XOR-loop region size derived from wrong byte
description: end = dest_addr + u64::from(data[i+1]) treats the low byte of the imm32 counter as the region length, yielding incorrect sizes.

title: Rol/Ror dispatch swapped
description: SmcAlgorithm::Rol calls ror8 and SmcAlgorithm::Ror calls rol8, contradicting the documented `byte = rol/ror(byte, key)` semantics.

title: XOR opcode-extension mask wrong in extract_key_from_block
description: Uses `block[i+1] & 0x30 == 0x30` which matches many unrelated ModR/M bytes; should mask 0x38 like trace() does.

title: ADD-loop ModR/M mask too loose
description: `data[i+1] & 0xF8 == 0x00` accepts ModR/M bytes 0x00-0x07 shared by other `80 /reg` opcodes, causing false ADD region detections.

title: JNZ relative jump cast wraps usize on negative result
description: `(pc as i64 + 2 + offset as i64) as usize` silently wraps for backward jumps and depends on the outer bound to avoid OOB indexing.

title: reconstruct() unchecked address arithmetic
description: `base_addr + i as u64` is unchecked and wraps when base_addr is near u64::MAX, producing incorrect memory_map lookups.

title: Poly1305 process_block uses wrong limb stride
description: Reads `buf[i*3..i*3+4]` instead of the standard 26-bit-limb extraction from buf[0..16]+pad, producing incorrect MAC values that break authentication.

title: Off-by-one in scan_constants loop on tiny inputs
description: `for i in 0..data.len()-3` underflows the iteration intent when len==4 is fine but panics on len<4 was guarded with <4; however `data.len()-3` on len exactly 3 would underflow — guard is `<4` so ok, but `saturating_sub(64)` window loop iterates `0..0` for len==64 missing the only valid window.

title: Big-endian word matched against same constant list causes spurious detections
description: Matching both LE and BE words against the same constant set yields false positives at offsets where reversed bytes coincidentally equal a constant.

title: `saturating_sub(64)` excludes the final valid 64-byte window
description: For `data.len()==64` the loop `0..0` runs zero times and misses the single window that could contain all four constants.

title: FNV hash collision treated as identical
description: `similarity()` returns 1.0 when only hashes match without verifying bytes, so any FNV (`simple_hash`) collision produces a false-positive Identical match.

title: Hash-only function matching trusts non-cryptographic FNV
description: Pass-1 pairs functions purely by `fp.hash` equality without comparing `bytes`, so collisions yield wrong cross-binary pairings reported as Identical.

title: lcs_similarity silently caps inputs at 512 bytes
description: Functions identical only in their first 512 bytes return similarity 1.0; remaining bytes are ignored, producing false Identical/Renamed matches for large functions.

title: instr_count set to byte length
description: `instr_count = bytes.len()` assumes 1 byte per instruction, which is wrong for x86 (variable) and ARM (4 bytes); downstream metrics are off by large factors.

title: Unchecked end-start subtraction in const size()
description: `(self.end_addr - self.start_addr) as usize` panics or wraps if `end_addr < start_addr` and also truncates on 32-bit targets for very large blocks.

title: Instruction size cast to u8 truncates
description: `bytes.len() as u8` silently truncates the stored `size` when an instruction's byte vector exceeds 255 bytes (e.g. synthetic/fuzz inputs), losing information used elsewhere.

title: md_index wrapping_mul produces near-random u64
description: `for _ in 0..exp` with exp up to 60 and base up to 19 overflows via `wrapping_mul` so similar functions yield wildly different md_index values, defeating the similarity metric.

title: unwrap_or(&0) hides missing call-graph node weight
description: `self.call_graph.node_weight(e.target()).unwrap_or(&0)` silently returns address 0 instead of erroring, causing phantom "call to 0x0" entries that can corrupt later matching.

title: jz/jne/jnz all assigned prime 211
description: Three distinct mnemonics share the same prime (211), so the prime-product loses identification power for these conditional jumps and inflates false matches.

title: md_index prime exponentiation wraps to near-random u64
description: wrapping_mul of base up to 19 by exp up to 60 overflows u64, so md_index_similarity exponential decay operates on essentially random values and the 0.10 weight component is noise.

title: duplicate prime 211 for jne/jz/jnz
description: three distinct mnemonics share prime 211, collapsing them in the prime-product hash and producing false-positive block matches.

title: unwrap_or(&0) silently returns address 0 for missing node weight
description: petgraph node_weight failure is masked as call target 0x0, polluting call_targets/callers_of results and downstream propagation/heuristics.

title: partial_cmp NaN treated as Equal in max_by
description: a NaN-scored candidate can win the max_by comparison and be accepted as a structural match above threshold.

title: matched_count = matches.len() - identical is fragile
description: relies on invariant identical<=matches.len(); a future refactor that counts identical from a different source would underflow usize.

title: propagate_matches only fires when both sides have exactly one callee
description: skipping all multi-callee functions makes call-graph propagation nearly useless on real binaries and silently drops obvious matches.

title: Loop detection uses branch source vs prev instruction
description: Compares branch instruction's own address to previous instruction address instead of branch target, so back-edges (loops) are never detected since instr.address > prev_addr always.

title: NormalizedFunction reads u32 LE but compares against u64 64-bit address
description: For 64-bit binaries with high base addresses, the u32-extended value can never fall in [base-4M, base+4M], so address-normalization silently does nothing.

title: CFG branch destination computed via i64 then truncated to u32
description: `(i as i64 + advance as i64 + rel) as u32` truncates and wraps on negative/large results, corrupting CFG edge hash.

title: While loop advances by 1 on mismatch causing O(n) overlapping rescans
description: Scanner re-examines overlapping 4-byte windows with no skip optimization; on adversarial input could be slow, and zeroed regions may chain-match neighboring patterns unexpectedly.

title: Overlap check uses new_bytes len but revert uses original_bytes len
description: PatchSet::add checks overlap using new_bytes.len() while revert_from writes original_bytes.len() bytes, so patches whose original/new differ in size can overlap on revert and corrupt the buffer.

title: Silent patch drop on out-of-bounds
description: PatchSet::apply_to silently skips patches whose end exceeds buffer.len() and only counts applied ones, returning a misleading success without signaling partial failure.

title: Hardcoded offset increments produce invalid CIL offsets
description: generate_body increments offset by 1 per ldarg (wrong for ldarg.s which is 2 bytes) and by 5 for call but call token is 4 bytes plus 1 opcode—nonetheless ldarg.s mis-sizing makes offsets non-monotonic/wrong for downstream consumers.

title: ReplaceRange ignores new instruction offsets
description: ReplaceRange retains instrs outside [start,end) then inserts new ones without rewriting their offsets, leaving duplicate or out-of-order offsets that break subsequent offset-based edits.

title: ImplMap import_scope=0 underflow
description: `im.import_scope as usize - 1` panics in debug / wraps in release when import_scope is 0, which is a legal "no module" sentinel.

title: ForwardedType ignores Implementation coded tag
description: `et.implementation >> 2` is used as an AssemblyRef index without checking the low 2 bits, so File/ExportedType implementations get misresolved to wrong AssemblyRef rows.

title: resolve_method_token ignores table tag
description: Token's high byte (0x06 for MethodDef) is masked off without verification, so a TypeDef/Field token silently returns a wrong MethodDef row.

title: UserString silently drops trailing odd byte
description: `chunks_exact(2)` discards a leftover byte when (len-1) is odd, producing a truncated/incorrect UTF-16 string instead of an error.

title: Stream end computed without overflow check
description: `base + offset + size` as usize can wrap on crafted PE input before the `end > data.len()` check, allowing an out-of-bounds slice.

title: SpecEventLogger::spawn panics if called twice
description: `.expect("SpecEventLogger::spawn called more than once")` panics in library code instead of returning a Result.

title: RwLock unwrap will panic on poison
description: Every `.unwrap()` on std `RwLock`/`Mutex` (lines 580,588,597,607,621,668,670,679,684,690,694,728,730,769,770,853,862,894,900,910,911,938,941,969) propagates panics from any poisoned lock, taking down unrelated subsystems.

title: event_count linear scan instead of HashMap lookup
description: `event_count` iterates the entire counters map with `.find` instead of `.get(variant_name)`, O(n) per call and unnecessary.

title: RingBuf::new panics on huge capacity
description: `capacity.next_power_of_two()` panics if `capacity > usize::MAX/2 + 1`, an unchecked input from public `new`.

title: Magic-bytes comparison wrong length
description: `data[0..4] == b"IDASGN"` compares 4 vs 6 bytes, always false, so v6+ files only detected via legacy 0x54/0x4A path.

title: Header length check off-by-two
description: Check is `< offset + 26` but code reads `data[offset+27]` at line 546 and slices `..offset+27` at 544, panicking on minimally-sized inputs.

title: Silent CRC truncation accepts short buffers
description: `crc_end = (crc_start + crc_length).min(data.len())` computes CRC over a shortened range, then compares against expected CRC of full length — can produce false matches or incorrect rejections instead of failing cleanly.

title: Unchecked addition of attacker-controlled lengths
description: `crc_start + pat.crc_length as usize` can overflow on 32-bit hosts when `pat.crc_length` (u16) plus offset is crafted via deserialized data; should use `checked_add`.

title: `partial_cmp().unwrap()` on f64 confidence
description: If a NaN sneaks into `confidence.combined` (e.g. from division), the sort comparator panics in library code.

title: Wrong CRC polynomial vs lib.rs crc16_flirt
description: This module's crc16_flirt uses poly 0xA001 (CRC-16-ARC) while lib.rs uses 0x8408 (true FLIRT poly), so apply_engine will reject every valid FLIRT pattern's CRC.

title: Inconsistent CRC region offset calculation
description: apply_engine computes `crc_off = fn_offset + crc_offset` while lib.rs uses `fn_offset + pat_len + crc_offset`, so the two engines hash different bytes for the same signature.

title: CRC check silently skipped when buffer too short
description: When `crc_end > data.len()` the CRC verification is skipped instead of treated as failure, allowing unverified matches near buffer end (also at lines 508, 561, 1354, 1392).

title: expect() in public library function build_ac_index
description: Public API panics on builder error instead of returning Result, propagating panics into callers.

title: Unchecked mask/bytes length mismatch in WildcardPattern::from_signature
description: Indexes `sig.mask[i]` without verifying `mask.len() == bytes.len()`, panicking on user-constructed FlirtSignature with mismatched vectors.

title: compute_favorites uses coverage_bits as bit-index proxy
description: `favored_bits[bits_count]` indexes by hit count rather than which bits are covered, so set-cover is meaningless and most entries with same coverage_bits are not favored.

title: next_usize truncates u64 to usize on 32-bit before modulo
description: `(self.next_u64() as usize) % n` on 32-bit platforms discards high bits, biasing distribution and making `next_usize` non-uniform for large n.

title: ForkServer.next_pid increments without wrap check
description: `self.next_pid += 1` will panic in debug on overflow after long runs; should use wrapping_add or u64.

title: select_sequential asserts non-empty queue
description: Library API panics rather than returning Result/Option, easy to trip from outside callers.

title: Dictionary load_afl_format mishandles quoted strings with escapes
description: Inner `&line[1..line.len()-1]` is taken as raw bytes; AFL dict format supports `\xNN` escapes which are silently kept literal, producing incorrect tokens.

title: AflQueue.next_id increments without overflow check
description: `self.next_id += 1` panics in debug on u64 wrap; trivially unreachable but still an unchecked arithmetic op flagged by lints.

title: Wrong nth() index parsing BB count
description: `line.split_whitespace().nth(2)` returns "bbs" not the count N for "BB Table: N bbs", so bb_count is parsed from the wrong token and silently becomes 0.

title: Inconsistent DRcov BB on-disk layout vs V2 parser
description: DrcovFile::parse reads `[module_id u16][start u32][size u16]` while DrcovBasicBlock::parse_bb_table (and the documented spec at L1297) reads `[start u32][size u16][module_id u16]`, so the two parsers decode the same bytes into completely different fields.

title: CRLF breaks DrcovHeader byte-offset accounting
description: `consumed += version_line.len() + 1` assumes a single '\n' terminator, but `str::lines()` also strips '\r\n'; on CRLF files the returned `hdr_consumed` is short by one byte per line, corrupting downstream slicing.

title: locate_binary_start misses last position
description: The loop bound `data.len().saturating_sub(marker_bytes.len())` is exclusive, so a marker placed at the very last possible offset is not found.

title: absolute_addr can wrap on high module bases
description: `module_base + u64::from(self.start)` performs unchecked addition; with adversarial input near `u64::MAX` it silently wraps.

title: fuzz() force-pushes 4-byte zero seed when queue empty
description: when no seeds provided, the default empty-queue path silently injects a 4-byte zero input instead of returning LibFuzzerError::EmptySeedPool, masking misconfiguration.

title: CrashSignalHandler uses expect("mutex poisoned") on every accessor
description: a single panic-while-locked permanently poisons the mutex and turns every subsequent crash-handler call (including is_crashed during recording) into a process panic in a fuzzer that is specifically designed to survive crashes.

title: fuzz_iteration panics with divide-by-zero/modulo-zero if corpus is empty
description: `self.stats.iterations as usize % self.corpus.len()` panics when corpus is empty; new() seeds with one entry but any caller clearing the corpus then calling fuzz_iteration crashes the harness.

title: StructuredInput::serialize silently truncates field lengths >65535 via `as u16`
description: fields longer than 65535 bytes are written with a truncated 16-bit length, producing a corrupted stream that deserialize will misparse without error.

title: InputSplicer::splice truncates 64-bit RNG to usize before modulo on 32-bit targets
description: `(rng.next_u64() as usize) % a.len()` truncates high bits on 32-bit platforms, biasing splice positions and silently changing fuzzing distribution across targets.

title: run_one derives "coverage" from fnv1a hash of input not real coverage
description: using fnv1a(input).to_le_bytes() as the only signal means the coverage map and CoverageFilter cannot distinguish inputs that actually exercise different code paths, defeating coverage-guided fuzzing entirely.

title: memcpy bound check underflows on n=0
description: `dst + n as u64 - 1` underflows to u64::MAX when n is 0, making is_accessible check meaningless and missing real overflows.

title: strcpy size check can overflow usize
description: `src_len + 1 > dst_size` wraps when src_len == usize::MAX, bypassing the overflow detection that is the whole point of this fortify check.

title: poison range computation overflows on high addrs
description: `addr + size` is unchecked u64 add inside `poison`/`unpoison`/`is_access_valid`, panicking in debug and silently wrapping in release for near-u64::MAX addresses.

title: hardcoded granule ignores configured scale_shift
description: `poison`/`unpoison`/`is_access_valid` use literal `granule = 8u64` instead of `self.map`'s `granule_size()`, so non-default scale_shift values produce wrong shadow indices vs `shadow_addr_for`.

title: UAF early-return misfires on reallocated address
description: `self.freed.contains(&addr)` returns UseAfterFree even after `track_alloc` reuses the same base address, because `freed` is never cleared on realloc.

title: heap access bound math can wrap u64
description: `addr + size as u64` and `alloc.addr + alloc.size as u64` in check_heap_access have no checked_add, so crafted huge addr/size values wrap and bypass the overflow detection.

title: Redo clears its own stack via inner write/insert/delete
description: `apply_command` calls `self.write/insert/delete` which each call `self.redo.clear()`, so after one redo the remaining redo history is wiped, breaking redo semantics.

title: kmp_search empty-needle returns n+1 zero-length matches
description: Returning `(0..=haystack.len()).collect()` yields an offset == data.len() that callers use to slice `data[offset..]`, risking later OOB and producing nonsensical FindMatch entries.

title: read_exact `offset + len` can overflow usize
description: `if offset + len > self.data.len()` wraps to a small value on large inputs and lets the subsequent `self.data[offset..offset+len]` panic instead of erroring.

title: find_hex_pattern slices token by byte index
description: `t.len() == 2` is byte length; a 2-byte UTF-8 token like "é" passes the check but `&t[..1]` slices mid-codepoint and panics in library code.

title: select(start,end) inverts range when end==start
description: `e.saturating_sub(1)` makes cursor < anchor for empty selection, so `range()` becomes `[e-1, s+1)` instead of empty.

title: annotations_overlapping `offset+len` can overflow
description: Unchecked addition can wrap with large `len`, mis-filtering annotations or panicking later.

title: Negative offset cast wraps to huge usize
description: `as_int().unwrap_or(0) as usize` on a negative i64 wraps to near-usize::MAX, bypassing bounds intent and producing IndexOutOfBounds with misleading offset.

title: Unchecked add can overflow
description: `off + 2 > self.data.len()` and `off + 4 > self.data.len()` overflow if off is near usize::MAX (reachable via negative i64 cast at line 626/635), defeating the bounds check.

title: Wrong alignment formula for non-power-of-two sizes
description: `align = size.min(8).max(1)` uses raw size as alignment; for size=3 (e.g. 3-byte array) align=3 produces non-power-of-two alignment and incorrect padding via `(align - offset % align) % align`.

title: sizeof array multiplication overflows silently
description: `elem_size * *count as i64` can overflow i64 with large count and is unchecked, producing wrong sizes for big arrays.

title: read_builtin offset+size overflow
description: `offset + size > data.len()` overflows if offset near usize::MAX, bypassing the bounds check before slicing.

title: Array field with missing size silently treated as 1
description: `field.array_size.unwrap_or(1)` masks parse failures so an array whose size couldn't be parsed gets length 1 with no warning.

title: array count parse defaults to 1 silently swallowing parse errors
description: `count_str.parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(1)` masks malformed array sizes (e.g. `byte arr[abc]`) as a 1-element array instead of raising a parse error.

title: offset += size as u64 can wrap on pathological size_t but more importantly `self.offset as usize + size` truncates on 32-bit hosts
description: On 32-bit targets, casting u64 offset to usize truncates silently, allowing reads at wrong addresses when offset > u32::MAX.

title: format_printf substitutes %s/%d in wrong order
description: The loop picks whichever of %s or %d appears first across all args independent of arg type, so `format_printf("%d %s", &["1","x"])` substitutes %d with "1" then %s with "x" correctly, but `format_printf("%s %d", &["1","x"])` substitutes %s→"1", %d→"x" — args are positional not type-checked, can mis-format.

title: usize cast of u64 offset truncates on 32-bit targets
description: `self.offset as usize + size` silently truncates large offsets on 32-bit hosts, enabling reads at wrong addresses without an EndOfData error.

title: array size parse error silently becomes count=1
description: `count_str.parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(1)` swallows malformed array bounds (e.g. `byte arr[N]` where N is a non-literal) and produces a 1-element array instead of a parse error.

title: remove() rebuilds index without clearing it first
description: After `self.index.remove(id)` and `entries.remove(idx)`, the loop re-inserts ids→new indices but never clears the map, so any id that no longer exists (none here, but fragile) or any id whose old index lingered would stay; combined with O(n) Vec::remove this is also a perf footgun on large libs.

title: format_printf substitutes %s/%d positionally not by arg type
description: It replaces the first occurrence of either %s or %d for each arg regardless of which specifier corresponds to which value, producing wrong output when the format string mixes specifiers in an unexpected order.

title: str::from_utf8 unwrap in hex-chunk parsing
description: `std::str::from_utf8(c).unwrap()` in parse_hex (template_library.rs:547) cannot panic given the ascii-hexdigit filter, but an unwrap remains in library code with no SAFETY comment, brittle to refactor.

title: CompressionTransform undo silently corrupts data
description: undo() for non-reversible transforms falls back to apply_inverse which defaults to apply(), so undoing a gzip-header strip re-applies the strip (or no-ops if magic gone) instead of restoring the original 10 bytes.

title: RotTransform inverse panics on i8::MIN
description: `-(self.amount)` on an i8 overflows when amount is i8::MIN, causing a debug-mode panic in apply_inverse.

title: Unbounded iteration over annotation range
description: `for i in ann.offset..ann.offset+ann.len` iterates the full annotation length before filtering, so a huge `len` causes a multi-second hang/overflow per render call.

title: Stale entropy cache when bytes_per_row changes
description: `row_entropy` caches results keyed only by presence, so altering `config.bytes_per_row` without calling invalidate_entropy returns entropy computed with the old block size.

title: b64_decode silently drops trailing partial chunk
description: A 1-char trailing chunk yields no output and no error, so corrupt base64 inputs decode to truncated data without indication.

title: DivU/ModU emitted with signed C operator
description: HlilExpr::DivU/ModU print as `/`/`%` producing signed C division and wrong results for unsigned semantics.

title: Sar emitted identically to Shr
description: Arithmetic right shift Sar is printed as `>>` with no signed cast, yielding implementation-defined behavior in C identical to logical Shr.

title: Const printed without respecting unsigned type
description: `format!("{value}")` prints raw i64 so unsigned-typed constants emerge as negatives in decompiled C output.

title: ConstantFolding ignores second operand width
description: Folds use only operand a's width and skip masking, so mixed-width Add/Sub/Mul/BitOps silently truncate or sign-extend incorrectly.

title: Mask computation underflows when bits==0
description: `(1u64 << w) - 1` panics in debug / underflows in release when an Int has bits==0, which is reachable via untrusted HlilType.

title: usize change count cast to u32
description: `candidates.len() as u32` silently truncates pass change counts on very large functions (and similar casts at 4082/4099/4120/4141).

title: SRA modelled as logical Shr
description: Z80 SRA (arithmetic right shift) preserves sign bit but the lifter emits IrExpr::Shr (logical), losing the sign-extension semantics.

title: ROR CF when count==0 reads wrong bit
description: The ("cf","ror") branch has no n==0 guard, so a zero count returns bit(v, w-1) instead of leaving CF unchanged, contradicting Intel SDM.

title: Byte slice on potentially non-ASCII mnemonic
description: &without_s[without_s.len()-2..] will panic if the mnemonic contains a multibyte UTF-8 char at the boundary.

title: Silent `as u8` truncation of align
description: parse_u64(v).unwrap_or(0) as u8 silently truncates align values >255 to a wrong low byte instead of erroring.

title: Unwrap after match guard is redundant but fragile
description: operand_list.first().unwrap() after a Some(Operand::Memory{..}) match relies on pattern guarantees; harmless today but a refactor that adds an if-guard would turn this into a panic in lib code.

title: Rol/Ror shift-by-bit-width panic
description: When eval_expr(r) % bits == 0, lv >> (bits - shift) shifts by full bit-width which is undefined-behavior shift and panics in debug.

title: Memory read addr+i can overflow u64
description: read() computes addr + i as u64 without wrapping/checked add, panicking on near-u64::MAX addresses in debug builds.

title: alloc_addr unchecked add
description: next_addr += 4 in const fn without wrapping or checked addition will panic on overflow after many allocations.

title: Length-to-size widening loses precision intent
description: size: self.length as usize stores byte length into a size field, conflating byte-length with semantic Size — likely a logic error where the wrong field is being populated.

title: Page mask assumes power-of-two page_size
description: addr & !(page_size - 1) produces wrong page index when page_size is not a power of two; no validation enforces this invariant on MemoryState construction.

title: BlockBuilder.end set to start address
description: build() sets end = Address::new(self.start) ignoring instruction extents, so block end is always equal to start and downstream range checks will be wrong.

title: Dominance-frontier walks through u32::MAX
description: If idom[&b.id] stays u32::MAX (unreachable block) the while runner != idom[&b.id] loop indexes idom[&u32::MAX] and panics or never terminates.

title: Shl/Shr ignore operand Size
description: Constant folding shifts a full u64 and does not truncate to the declared Size, producing wrong constants for Byte/Word/DWord operands.

title: Const-fold Shl masks shift by 63 regardless of Size
description: a << (b & 63) can shift past the operand width for 32/16/8-bit sizes and never truncates the result, yielding incorrect folded constants.

title: CSE keyed on Debug formatting
description: Using format!("{src:?}") as the CSE hash key is fragile (Debug output not guaranteed stable) and ignores size/type info ambiguities, risking incorrect substitutions.

title: Worklist value unused in const-prop
description: pop_front discards the variable and rescans every instruction each iteration, giving O(n*defs) work and never marking partially-known phis as non-constant, so propagation can be incomplete.

title: elf_arch_hint OOB index
description: checks bytes.len() < 19 then indexes bytes[19], panicking when input length is exactly 19.

title: ext2 magic check off-by-one
description: guard bytes.len() >= 1080 still indexes bytes[1081], panicking for inputs of length 1080 or 1081.

title: unchecked base+offset add
description: base + reloc.offset_in_image can overflow u64 and panic in debug builds for attacker-controlled offsets.

title: MipsHi16 unchecked add
description: full + 0x8000 is a plain u64 add that panics in debug when full is near u64::MAX after wrapping_add_signed.

title: unchecked file_offset+delta
description: self.file_offset + delta can overflow u64 for crafted segment metadata, panicking in debug builds.

title: GnuHashTable::lookup panics when nbuckets is 0
description: hash % self.nbuckets panics if a malformed .gnu.hash section has nbuckets=0 (no validation in parse64).

title: GnuBloomFilter::might_contain panics if word_bits is 0
description: self.word_bits - 1 underflows and hash / self.word_bits divides by zero; constructor accepts any u32.

title: get_section_name_table can overflow on 32-bit usize
description: off + sz adds two attacker-controlled section header fields without checked_add, can wrap and cause a panic on slicing.

title: Shdr32/64::parse_all overflows on attacker-controlled e_shoff/e_shnum
description: e_shoff as usize + i * step is unchecked; on 32-bit usize a large e_shoff and big e_shnum wrap silently, producing wrong parses.

title: num_size silently defaults when truncated
description: data.get(10).copied().unwrap_or(8) masks truncation since MIN_SIZE=12 already guarantees len>=12 but is_integer_num at idx 11 similarly defaults with unwrap_or(false), hiding malformed input.

title: integer overflow in offset+n_bytes bounds check
description: *offset + n_bytes and *offset + slen can wrap on attacker-controlled offset, bypassing the bounds check (use checked_add).

title: read_lua_string slen cast u64->usize on 32-bit
description: as usize truncates a 64-bit length silently on 32-bit platforms, then read_bytes pos+n can also overflow, allowing under-read of huge declared strings.

title: unbounded recursion in parse_51_52/parse_53_54
description: nested protos are parsed recursively without depth limit; crafted bytecode with deeply nested protos crashes the loader with stack overflow.

title: LuaEndian::from_byte treats every non-zero as LE
description: Lua spec uses 1 for LE and 0 for BE; any other corrupt value silently becomes LE instead of erroring, masking malformed headers.

title: VersionReport endianness wrong default
description: byte 6 == 1 -> little else big, so any non-1 value (including corrupt 2) reports big, inconsistent with LuaEndian::from_byte (non-zero=LE) elsewhere in the crate.

title: Fat binary nfat endianness inverted
description: When magic equals FAT_CIGAM (little-endian-read of canonical big-endian on-disk header) the code reads nfat as LE, but the comment correctly notes the fat header is always big-endian; the branches are swapped, yielding a byte-swapped slice count.

title: read_u32_le off+4 can panic
description: off + 4 is computed before the slice get, so an attacker-controlled off near usize::MAX (or large file-offset cast) overflows usize and panics rather than returning None.

title: parse_method_list hard-codes little-endian
description: Method list flags/count/relative-offsets are read as from_le_bytes regardless of binary endianness, mis-parsing ObjC metadata in any big-endian Mach-O (PowerPC).

title: Relative-method selector base address wrong
description: sel_va = offset + sel_rel uses the in-buffer offset as base; the on-disk Apple format makes the relative pointer relative to the field VM address, so get_string(sel_va) will resolve incorrect VAs.

title: read_cstr off + max_len can overflow usize
description: let end = off + max_len is computed without checked/saturating add before .min(bytes.len()), allowing a panic on hostile inputs where caller supplies large offsets.

title: endstream-not-found silently treated as zero-length
description: windows(9).position(...).unwrap_or(0) makes a missing endstream produce length=0 and advance pos only by 9, corrupting all subsequent parsing.

title: /Length match collides with /Length1, /Length2
