description: parse_length_from_dict uses substring search for /Length with no delimiter check, so dictionaries containing /Length1 before /Length yield wrong stream lengths.

title: hex escape in name skipped at EOF
description: self.pos + 2 < self.data.len() should be <=; a valid #XX escape at the final two bytes of input is silently dropped.

title: Weighted policy ignores weights
description: Index (healthy.len() * 7 / 11) % healthy.len() is deterministic and unrelated to weights, so the Weighted policy never actually uses upstream weights.

title: block_on inside async-capable runtime
description: probe_server_tools_sync builds a current_thread runtime and calls block_on - if called from within an existing Tokio runtime this panics, breaking tool discovery.

title: PatchBytesTool offset+patch.len() can overflow usize
description: attacker-supplied `offset` (u64) is cast to usize then added to patch.len() without checked_add, causing wraparound and a subsequent out-of-bounds slice write or false bounds-check pass on 32-bit targets.

title: SectionDumpTool off+len wraps before bounds check
description: `off + len` (both user-controlled u64s cast to usize) can overflow, making `end > d.len()` falsely return false and panicking on slice or returning wrong region.

title: HexDumpTool off+len overflow before .min()
description: `off + len` is computed before `.min(data.len())`, so a large user `offset` plus default `len = data.len()` overflows usize and triggers undefined truncation/panic on the slice.

title: XorDecryptTool silently truncates 64-bit key to u8
description: `k as u8` drops high bits of the user-supplied `key` (u64) with no validation, so callers passing 0x100 get XOR with 0x00 instead of an error.

title: demangle_simple slices &s[..n] on UTF-8 boundaries
description: the parsed length `n` is treated as a byte offset but `s` may contain non-ASCII bytes, so `&s[..n]` panics on a non-char-boundary input rather than returning the original name.

title: base64_decode silently drops trailing partial chunks
description: chunks shorter than 4 are skipped with `break`, so malformed or unpadded base64 inputs return a truncated result instead of an error.

title: BMH skip table unsound for masked pattern bytes
description: skip table only records the literal `value` byte, leaving other bytes that satisfy the mask with the default full-length skip, causing valid matches to be skipped.

title: Unchecked u64 address+offset arithmetic in read/write
description: `addr.0 + i` and `addr.0 + i as u64` can wrap on near-u64::MAX addresses, silently aliasing reads/writes to low addresses in release builds.

title: `span()` panics or wraps when max key is u64::MAX
description: `Address::new(max + 1)` overflows when the largest stored byte is at u64::MAX, panicking in debug and wrapping to 0 in release.

title: Offset cast u64 to usize loses bits on 32-bit targets
description: `(addr - base) as usize` silently truncates large offsets on 32-bit builds, allowing out-of-bounds reads/writes to pass the subsequent bounds check.

title: Indexing assumes provider returned exact length
description: `bytes[0]` (and similar in u16/u32/u64 readers) will panic if a custom `MemoryProvider` returns a shorter `Vec` than requested, instead of returning `None`.

title: `current += bytes_this_page` can wrap u64 near address space end
description: Reads/writes spanning the top of the 64-bit address space wrap `current` to 0, causing an infinite loop or wrong-page lookups.

title: V2 PAGE_USE_EXTRA uses page_idx as extras index
description: Comment admits heuristic: use page_idx as index - correct dyld semantics require the extras index from the page_starts value masked, not page_idx, producing wrong/missing fixups.

title: V2 apply omits value_add when rebuilding pointer
description: Computes `(raw & value_mask) + slide` but ignores `v2.value_add`, so rebased pointers are off by value_add.

title: V2 EXTRA_END loop continuation inverted
description: Loop continues while `e & EXTRA_END == 0` is false; per dyld, `EXTRA_END` set means this is the LAST entry, so the loop should break when set.

title: V2 chain stride uses *4 for 64-bit pointers
description: `ptr_off += delta as usize * 4` - V2 uses 8-byte pointers, value_mask combined with line 492 yields wrong chain walking.

title: va_to_file_offset uses non-saturating add
description: `self.file_offset + (va - self.address)` can overflow if file_offset+size exceeds u64.

title: read_at_va integer overflow in slice index
description: `data.get(file_off..file_off + len)` can overflow usize for attacker-controlled `len`.

title: Fmt22x truncates 16-bit register vBBBB to 8 bits
description: format 22x stores BBBB as u8::try_from(word(1) & 0xff), mis-mapping register index >= 256.

title: Fmt32x truncates 16-bit registers vAAAA/vBBBB to 8 bits
description: both 16-bit register operands in 32x are masked with & 0xff and pushed as u8.

title: Fmt3rc register-range computation can panic on overflow
description: (cccc + u16::from(i)) & 0xff performs u16 addition that panics in debug.

title: fill-array-data size can overflow usize on 32-bit
description: num_elem * elem_width is unchecked usize multiplication of attacker-controlled DEX payload fields.

title: descriptor_to_type panics on multibyte UTF-8 after '['
description: &d[1..] slices a &str at byte 1; multibyte char causes panic.

title: block_at_offset misses bytes within the last instruction of a block
description: end is set to the start offset of the last instruction (not its end).

title: 30t/31t branch offsets zero-extend high word
description: (i32::from(word2) << 16) | i32::from(word1) uses unsigned conversion.

title: F11n-style literal decode is dead/wrong
description: nibble_b.cast_signed() >> 4 on a 4-bit value shifts only data bits out.

title: .locals treated as .registers
description: .locals N overwrites registers with N, but Dalvik registers_size = locals + ins_size.

title: Register numbers above 255 silently truncated
description: n & 0xff masks the parsed register index.

title: TCP checksum includes stale checksum field
description: to_bytes_no_checksum writes self.checksum at offset 16 instead of zero.

title: UDP checksum includes stale checksum field
description: checksum_ipv4 calls to_bytes() which embeds self.checksum.

title: Ipv4 dissector panics when ihl exceeds packet length
description: data[ihl..].to_vec() is unchecked.

title: TcpSegment::to_bytes_no_checksum panics for data_offset < 5
description: if data_offset below 5, hl < 20 and writes overflow buffer.

title: TCP next_protocol set to dst_port not application protocol
description: Storing dst port as next_protocol misroutes registry lookups.

title: UDP length silently truncated to u16::MAX for oversize payload
description: unwrap_or(u16::MAX) then saturating_add(8) under-reports length.

title: IPv4 parse slice OOB when total_len < ihl
description: bytes[ihl_bytes..end] panics because end < start.

title: TCP seq number compared with raw `<` ignores wrap
description: seg.seq < state.buffer.next_seq misclassifies across the 32-bit seq wrap.

title: Evict oldest stream picks arbitrary HashMap key
description: self.streams.keys().next() returns an unordered key.

title: Reassembled bytes duplicated and buffer never freed
description: buffer.data keeps growing and is copied wholesale into reassembled.data.

title: GapDetector ignores 32-bit seq wrap when merging ranges
description: start.wrapping_add(len) plus s <= last.1 produces wrong gaps when segment straddles wrap.

title: HTTP/2 frame length cast `length as usize` then silently clamped
description: 24-bit length clamped via .min(data.len()) so truncated frames accepted.

title: LenLt(0) underflows on `*n - 1`
description: *n - 1 where n is u32 panics in debug / wraps in release when filter is LenLt(0).

title: Net mask `!0u32 << (32 - prefix)` panics when prefix > 32
description: 32 - prefix underflows usize since prefix is u8 unchecked.

title: FilterCompiler Net mask shift panics when prefix > 32
description: Same unchecked 32 - prefix underflow in compiler path.

title: `ts_usec * 1000` can overflow u32 in Duration::new
description: Multiplying u32 ts_usec by 1000 overflows when ts_usec >= ~4.29M.

title: `read_u16/u32/i32` index without bounds checks
description: These helpers panic via direct indexing if callers miscompute offsets.

title: BPF VM `LenGt/LenLt` loads `u32::MAX` constant instead of packet length
description: Compiled length filters push LD_IMM u32::MAX never substituted.

title: LenLt(0) panics on unsigned subtract
description: *n - 1 underflows u32 when user constructs FilterExpr::LenLt(0).

title: Net mask shift panics for prefix>32
description: !0u32 << (32 - prefix) underflows usize subtract when prefix>32.

title: FilterCompiler Net mask shift panics for prefix>32
description: Same unchecked 32 - prefix underflow in compile path.

title: BPF length filters never load packet length
description: LenGt/LenLt compile to LD_IMM u32::MAX never replaced at runtime.

title: `ts_usec * 1000` overflows u32 in Duration::new
description: Multiplying the u32 microsecond field by 1000 overflows.

title: Pcre silently treats non-UTF8 payload as empty
description: from_utf8(&ctx.payload).unwrap_or() means binary payload skips PCRE matching.

title: Depth condition can overflow usize
description: current_depth = current_offset + *d has no checked add.

title: DSize comparison saturates payload size to u32::MAX
description: Payloads larger than 4GB silently clamp.

title: State count cast `goto.len() as u32` truncates before panic check
description: Cast happens unconditionally; on 64-bit overflow truncates.

title: EventProviderGuid Display emits non-standard GUID format

title: SysEnterPattern.matches accepts trailing bytes silently
description: `actual.len() < self.bytes.len()` rejects only short inputs; longer inputs match on prefix only, which may produce false positives when callers expect exact-length matching.

description: If a `ProcessInfo` has `ppid == pid`, parent_map maps the pid to itself causing infinite recursion and stack overflow.

description: `std::fs::read_dir` follows symlinks, so a symlinked directory cycle causes unbounded recursion and stack overflow.

title: `content_contains` reads entire file into memory
description: Reading arbitrarily large files via `std::fs::read` during walk enables OOM/DoS when scanning directories with huge files.

description: `pe_offset` is a `u32` from file bytes cast to usize; `pe_offset + 4` and later `opt_offset + 0x88` can wrap on 32-bit and bypass bounds checks; use checked_add.

title: Glob matcher has exponential backtracking

title: parent_domain mishandles multi-label TLDs
description: For "foo.example.co.uk" returns "co.uk", causing false-positive eTLD+1 matches across unrelated domains.

title: ip_prefix_24 accepts non-numeric octets
description: `split('.')` of arbitrary string passes len==4 check, so "a.b.c.d" produces "a.b.c" prefix, polluting correlation evidence.

title: read_response uses from_utf8_lossy on HTTP body

description: On `start > end` the error's `len` field is set to `max_seq` (last seq) rather than record count, misleading callers.

title: Wrong bit field for ETM4 exception EL
description: `el = ext & 0x03` reads bits [1:0] but ETM4 spec encodes Exception Level in bits [2:1], so EL is always reported wrong.

title: ULEB128 shift can exceed 63 silently

title: step_forward uses `.expect("just stored")` in library code
description: Unwrap on `Option` that was set one line above is sound today, but any future refactor to early-return on error would turn this into a library-level panic.

title: DataFlow query checks source-write position against sink-write set
description: A single event cannot simultaneously be a write to source_addr and a write to sink_addr, so this intersection is always empty (and ignores temporal ordering anyway).

title: CallChain ignores temporal order between from and to
description: It returns every Call-from event whenever ANY call-to-`to` exists anywhere in the trace, even before the call-from, so results are wrong.

title: Heap alloc/free classified by event index parity
description: Marking even-indexed calls as allocs and odd as frees is meaningless and produces bogus HeapOperationsReport data.

title: Unchecked subtraction in coverage range size
description: `e - s` panics in debug and wraps in release when a caller passes `(start, end)` with end < start.

title: Sequence matcher never resets on mismatch mid-sequence
description: Once pat_idx>0, a non-matching event is skipped instead of resetting/retrying, so interleaved noise within a sequence is silently tolerated and false positives are produced.

title: Memory access pattern analysis ignores access length
description: Uses only `addr >= start && addr < end`, so a read/write whose start sits just below `end` but extends into the range (or starts inside and spans past `end`) is mis-classified.

title: Nonce-counter wraparound check happens after use
description: fetch_add returns prior value so ctr==u32::MAX is checked after that nonce was already emitted, and the next call reuses counter 0 with the same salt, breaking ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce-uniqueness.

title: PerfEventCounter::read ignores short reads
description: read(2) may return 0<n<8 yet the code returns the partially-initialized u64 as the counter value, producing wrong instruction counts.

title: read_memory can fault past requested length
description: the PEEKDATA loop always reads a full word even when only a few trailing bytes are needed, so when addr+len sits just before an unmapped page the syscall faults and aborts a valid read.

title: Checkpoint counter silently saturates
description: position_counter uses saturating_add(1), so after u64::MAX checkpoints every further checkpoint collides on the same TtdPosition instead of erroring.

title: Nanosecond timestamp truncated to u64
description: `d.as_nanos() as u64` truncates the u128, narrowing salt entropy and making salt collisions more likely between concurrent encryptors built from the same key.

title: Output path built by string concatenation
description: `format!("{}/trace_{}.run", output_dir, n)` ignores trailing separators and never validates output_dir, allowing path-traversal-style names from caller-controlled config.

title: RunFileHeader::SIZE=72 but doc says 64 and parser only reads 64 bytes
description: Constant claims 72 bytes while only fields up through offset 64 are read/written, causing 8-byte misalignment when parser advances `pos` and subsequent reads land in the wrong place.

title: SequenceId::next can panic on overflow
description: `self.0 + 1` is unchecked and will panic in debug builds when sequence reaches u64::MAX; should use `wrapping_add` or `checked_add`.

title: mark_writes loses prior dirty bits and mishandles lower base
description: The condition `base_page > min_page || n_pages < new` rebuilds bitmap from scratch, discarding previously marked dirty pages, and if old base was below min_page it silently keeps the old (potentially smaller) bitmap missing new high pages.

title: mark_writes computes end_page with unchecked add
description: `addr + data.len() as u64` can overflow when an attacker-controlled write address is near u64::MAX, panicking in debug builds.

title: bytes_added not counted for new zero-filled pages
description: Added pages whose content equals the all-zero `empty` placeholder fail the `b_page != a_page` check, so they are silently dropped from the diff and byte counters.

title: Inner doc comments after items
description: `//!` doc comments at lines 16-22 appear after `pub mod` items, which is invalid Rust (inner attributes must precede all items) and will fail to compile.

title: Premature break assumes sorted events
description: `find_last_write_before` breaks on first `ev_tick >= tick` assuming events are tick-ordered, but `push_event` appends without sorting the events vec, so later writes with smaller ticks are missed.

title: Same unsorted-events break in find_last_write_range_before
description: Identical early-break bug: events vec is not enforced sorted by tick, so the function can return a stale "last" write.

title: current_tick set past replayed state
description: After the replay loop, `current_tick = target_tick` is assigned unconditionally in the else branch even when no event at target_tick was applied, making state inconsistent with reported tick.

title: Duplicate-tick events lose index entry
description: `push_event` skips inserting into `tick_index` when a tick collision occurs, so later events sharing a tick are unreachable via `first_event_at_or_after`, breaking seeks.

title: Unnecessary clone of entire event
description: `apply_event_forward` clones the whole `TraceEvent` (including all mem_writes Vec<u8>) just to satisfy the borrow checker, causing O(N) allocation per forward step on large traces.

title: StringCount condition ignores count value
description: `Condition::StringCount(id)` returns `len() > 0`, identical to `StringMatch`, so any rule using `#id == N` semantics is broken.

title: parse_string_value panics on short/non-ASCII text
description: `raw.find('"').unwrap_or(raw.len()-1) + 1` underflows when raw is empty and slices on non-char boundaries when the value contains multibyte UTF-8, causing a panic in library code.

title: Condition parser has inverted operator precedence
description: `parse_condition_text` checks ` and ` before ` or ` via `splitn`, ignoring left-to-right precedence and parenthesisation, producing wrong boolean trees for non-trivial conditions.

title: Recursive directory walk follows symlinks
description: `walk_dir_for_rules` and `walk_scan` recurse on `path.is_dir()` without checking symlinks, allowing infinite loops or path traversal out of the intended tree.

title: scan_directory loads every file fully into RAM
description: `walk_scan` calls `std::fs::read(&path)` on every regular file with no size cap, so a single large file in a scanned tree exhausts memory.

title: partial_cmp().unwrap() panics on NaN confidence
description: Sorting/`max_by` on `Confidence` floats unwraps `partial_cmp`, which returns None for NaN and panics in library code.

title: top_hypothesis panics on NaN confidence
description: Same NaN-unwrap pattern in `max_by`; a single NaN-valued hypothesis crashes the reasoning engine.

title: usize→u32 token estimate truncates on large histories
description: `(chars / 4) as u32` silently wraps when summed message content exceeds ~16 GiB/4, producing wrong token estimates that may bypass limits.

title: Unchecked byte-slice on user content can panic
description: `content[start + 2..end]` slices arbitrary template content without char-boundary or order checks; multibyte chars or a `}}` appearing before `{{` cause a panic in library code.

title: find("}}") returns position relative to start of content, not after `{{`
description: `content.find("}}")` searches the whole content from index 0, so a `}}` earlier in the string yields `end < start`, producing an empty/invalid var name or panicking slice.

title: usize→i64 cast on `limit` can wrap on 128-bit-style overflows / negative interpretation
description: `limit as i64` will silently wrap if `limit > i64::MAX`, producing a negative SQL LIMIT that errors at runtime rather than being validated.

title: f64→u32 cast saturates silently
description: `(chars / 4.0).ceil() as u32` truncates/saturates for very large inputs (>~17GB chars) without warning; minor but unchecked.

title: Rate-limiter purge only trims contiguous old entries from front
description: If timestamps are pushed out of monotonic order (clock skew), older entries behind a newer front are never purged, inflating throttle counts.

title: run_id collision under concurrent runs
description: run_id is `workflow_id-epoch_ms` with millisecond precision; concurrent or rapid runs of the same workflow collide and `INSERT OR REPLACE` silently overwrites the prior run's record.

title: critical-path marks only longest endpoints
description: `is_critical = d == max_duration` flags only branches whose longest-path total equals the max, so only the path's terminal node(s) get marked critical instead of every branch on the critical path.

title: Rollback returns RollbackFailed on successful rollback
description: After successfully rolling back completed steps the engine returns `WorkflowError::RollbackFailed`, misclassifying a successful rollback as a rollback failure and hiding the real cause.

title: apply_output silently masks unknown keys
description: Unrecognised output_mapping keys are inserted as the literal string `"unmapped:<key>"` instead of producing an error, so workflow misconfiguration is silently propagated as data.

title: Persistence errors silently discarded
description: All `store.add_workflow`/`update_step_result`/`set_workflow_status` calls inside `run()` use `let _ =`, so DB failures (disk full, lock contention) are dropped and state diverges from reality.

title: Hardcoded 4-byte stack slot width
description: stack_arg_count = (offset/4)+1 assumes 32-bit slots and yields wrong/inflated counts on x64/arm64 where stack slots are 8 bytes.

title: MS x64 unreachable due to subset arg-register match
description: ms_x64 arg regs (rcx,rdx,r8,r9) are a subset of sysv arg regs, so sysv_matches >= ms_matches always, making "ms_x64" branch only selectable via Equal->"unknown" — Windows x64 is never detected.

title: Misleading score comment vs behavior
description: Comment says "bonus for matching" but condition rewards inequality; correctness OK but trap for future edits — also adds flat +5 regardless of whether stack args even exist, biasing scores for register-only functions.

title: Redundant unsigned_abs after clamp(0,100)
description: score is already clamped non-negative so unsigned_abs is dead code and obscures intent.

title: LinearSweep ignores entry_addr leader
description: `current_start = instrs[0].address` instead of `entry_addr`, so when entry differs from first instruction address the entry block is mis-keyed and CFG entry address doesn't match any block.

title: Recursive dfs_post can blow the stack
description: `dfs_post` recurses per successor with no depth limit; large CFGs (MAX_BLOCKS=65536) will overflow the thread stack.

title: CycleDetector::dfs recursive without depth bound
description: Same recursive pattern on potentially 65K-block CFGs will stack-overflow in library code called from any consumer.

title: RecursiveDescent drops CallDest successors
description: The `_ =>` fallthrough arm handles CallDest correctly, but `CallDest` terminator semantics never schedule the call target or fall-through when `follow_calls` config would expect it—config is also entirely unused.

title: read_uint off+size may overflow usize
description: `off + size > data.len()` can wrap on attacker-controlled `off` near `usize::MAX`, bypassing the bounds check and indexing OOB.

title: decode_absolute_table index arithmetic can overflow
description: `start + i * entry_size as usize` is unchecked; with `max_entries=4096` and large `start` from a huge `table_addr - data_base`, the multiplication or addition can wrap and silently read wrong memory regions.

title: LinearSweep ignores entry_addr when seeding first block
description: current_start is set to instrs[0].address rather than entry_addr, so when entry differs from the first instruction the entry block start is wrong and ReconstructedCfg.entry no longer matches any block key.

title: Recursive dfs_post has no depth bound
description: Plain recursion over up to MAX_BLOCKS (65,536) nodes can overflow the default thread stack in library code with no guard or iterative fallback.

title: CycleDetector::dfs is unbounded recursion
description: Same recursive pattern over the full CFG will stack-overflow on deep chains, panicking library consumers (e.g. via CfgSummary::from_cfg).

title: CallDest terminator drops fall-through and ignores follow_calls config
description: The recursive-descent match has no CallDest arm, so calls fall into the default branch that wires a Fallthrough edge but never honors ReconstructionConfig.follow_calls, leaving call graphs silently incomplete.

title: read_uint bounds check can wrap
description: `off + size > data.len()` can overflow usize for adversarial off near usize::MAX, bypassing the bound and allowing the subsequent copy_from_slice to panic or read past intended limits.

title: decode_*_table index arithmetic unchecked
description: `start + i * entry_size as usize` is unchecked; with a large (table_addr-data_base) start and max_entries=4096, multiplication or addition can wrap usize and produce a misleading read offset before read_uint sees it.

title: SSA phi-arg fills wrong predecessor slot on CFG mismatch
description: `position(...).unwrap_or(0)` silently writes to predecessor index 0 when bb is not found in succ.pred, corrupting phi arguments instead of erroring.

title: Recursive dominator-tree walk can stack-overflow
description: `rename_block` recurses through dom-tree children despite the comment claiming iterative; deep CFGs (long if-else chains) overflow the thread stack.

title: Recursive preorder_walk can stack-overflow on deep dom trees
description: `preorder_walk` is implemented as direct recursion without depth limit; deeply dominated CFGs can blow the stack.

title: Induction-var stride computed without overflow check
description: `hi0 - lo0` on i64 ranges can overflow (e.g. range spanning i64::MIN..i64::MAX), producing wrong stride and bogus induction-variable detection.

title: partial_cmp unwrap on f32 confidence
description: NaN confidence in candidates causes `partial_cmp(...).unwrap()` to panic in library code during deduplication.

title: ClangSanitizerHeuristic accepts any 0x48 byte
description: Code checks `bytes[i] == 0x48` without filtering the following byte (comment says "48 8x"), so nearly every REX-prefixed instruction is mis-flagged as a prologue.

title: GCC canary heuristic reports wrong function start
description: Heuristic walks back a fixed 32 bytes (or i) and reports that as the function entry, which is almost never the true entry and yields incorrect addresses.

title: window_end saturating_add masks overflow as cluster
description: When `candidates[i]` is near u64::MAX, `window_end` saturates to MAX so all remaining candidates falsely appear within the window, producing a bogus PGO cluster.

title: OverlapDetector::find_overlaps assumes sorted input but does not verify
description: Method documents "sorted boundaries" and `break`s on `c.start >= end_i`, so unsorted input silently misses overlaps with no panic or error.

title: min_function_size leaves boundary end unset instead of dropping
description: When the estimated size is below `min_function_size`, the code leaves `end = None` but still emits the boundary, producing zero-size or unbounded boundaries downstream.

title: partial_cmp unwrap on NaN confidence
description: NaN in FunctionCandidate.confidence causes partial_cmp().unwrap() to panic during deduplicate in library code.

title: Sanitizer heuristic matches any 0x48 byte
description: Comment claims pattern "48 8x" but code only checks bytes[i]==0x48 without filtering the second byte, mis-flagging nearly every REX-prefixed instruction as a function prologue.

title: GCC canary reports wrong function entry
description: Heuristic walks back a fixed 32 bytes (or i) and reports that offset as the entry, which is almost never the true function start, producing incorrect addresses.

title: saturating_add masks overflow into bogus cluster
description: If candidates[i] is near u64::MAX, window_end saturates so every later candidate falsely appears within the window and is promoted as a PGO cluster.

title: find_overlaps silently relies on sorted input
description: The `break` on `c.start >= end_i` requires the slice to be sorted by start, but no precondition is checked or enforced, so unsorted callers silently miss overlaps.

title: sub-min-size boundary emitted with end=None
description: When estimated size is below min_function_size the boundary is still pushed but with end=None, producing apparently-unbounded boundaries downstream instead of being dropped.

title: Multibyte XOR key extraction drops 0x00 bytes
description: The `*imm > 0` guard skips zero immediates so any key containing 0x00 is silently truncated, returning an incorrect/shorter key.

title: StackStore::bytes panics when size > 8
description: `le[..n]` with `n = self.size as usize` panics if size exceeds 8 (e.g., vector store), and the `size: u8` field is unvalidated by the constructor.

title: base64_decode accepts truncated input
description: The decoder silently terminates without verifying length is a multiple of 4 or proper padding, so corrupt/truncated base64 yields partial output presented as valid.

title: XOR key extraction ignores key=0x00 candidate
description: `*imm > 0` filter means a real XOR-by-zero (no-op encrypt) or 0x00-byte register load is treated as no key, instead of being reported.

title: Wrong offset for __si_class_type_info base typeinfo
description: Single-inheritance base ptr should be read at ti_rva + 2*ptr_size, not +2*ptr_size+4 — the `+4` is the vmi flags-skip and shifts the read by 4 bytes giving garbage base RVAs.

title: Unchecked u64 add in section scan loop
description: `addr + ptr_size <= section.start + section.size` can wrap on pathological section bounds yielding an infinite/incorrect loop; should use checked_add.

title: Slot scan walks past section end
description: `slot_addr += ptr_size` inside the vtable-extension loop never checks against `section.start + section.size`, so a section ending in code-pointer-like bytes can read out-of-section memory through `read_ptr`.

title: Misleading variable `type_desc_rva` holds absolute address
description: `image_base + rva32` is an absolute VA but the binding is named `_rva` and later passed to `is_rodata_address`; if `is_rodata_address` expects an RVA this silently mis-classifies, otherwise the name invites future bugs.

title: `max_id = v.0 + 1` can overflow u32
description: A caller-constructed `TypeVar(u32::MAX)` makes solve() panic in debug or wrap to 0 in release, defeating the explicit comment that this guards against out-of-bounds.

title: read failure silently treated as leaf typeinfo
description: `read_u32(flags_addr).unwrap_or(0)` converts a read error into "Leaf with no bases", hiding truncated/corrupt rodata as a valid parse instead of returning None.

title: meet uses wrong base for adjusted_hi
description: adjusted_hi is computed from `lo` instead of `adjusted_lo`, yielding incorrect/possibly out-of-range upper bound for the intersection.

title: join recomputes hi using stride truncation that can produce hi < input hi
description: `lo + ((hi - lo) / s * s)` truncates hi so the joined interval may not actually contain `other.hi`, violating the join (LUB) contract.

title: unwrap on iter min/max in si_mul
description: `unwrap()` on min/max is safe today but uses unwrap in a lib API; more importantly saturating_mul of i64::MIN * -1 saturates incorrectly producing wrong bounds.

title: read accepts entry_size > 8 and silently truncates
description: `n = entry_size as usize` with `buf = [0u8; 8]` will panic in `copy_from_slice` if entry_size > 8 because slice/buf size mismatch.

title: si_shr stride right-shift loses precision and uses .max(1) hiding zero
description: right-shifting the stride by `shift` then clamping to 1 silently produces an unsound stride approximation rather than recomputing from new lo/hi.

title: Base class array stride wrong for 64-bit RTTI
description: In 64-bit MSVC RTTI the base class array entries are i32 image-relative offsets (4 bytes), not ptr_size; using `ptr_size as u64` stride mis-indexes entries.

title: num_contained offset uses ptr_size
description: `addr + ptr_sz` assumes the i32 type-descriptor field is ptr-sized but in 64-bit RTTI it is always 4 bytes, causing wrong reads on 64-bit.

title: COL skip stride too small
description: `i += 20` after a match skips only 20 bytes but a 64-bit COL is 24 bytes (includes p_self), risking overlapping rematches.

title: ImageSection::end can overflow
description: `self.base + self.data.len() as u64` is not checked for u64 overflow and can wrap when base is near `u64::MAX`.

title: unwrap on try_into in scan
description: `u64::from_le_bytes(data[i..i+8].try_into().unwrap())` panics if invariants regress; should use safe slice reads in library code.

title: Validator below-threshold path can falsely validate
description: When `exec_fraction < 0.8` the returned score `exec_fraction * 0.5` can still meet a custom `min_function_fraction <= 0.4`, marking junk as validated.

title: Relative jump-table target computation truncates high addresses
description: Casting `base_addr as i64` truncates u64 addresses above i64::MAX (e.g. kernel-space) before adding the rel32, producing wrong targets.

title: read_ptr_le bounds check can wrap on huge offset
description: `off + n` is unchecked addition; a near-`usize::MAX` `off` overflows and bypasses the length check, then `data[off..off+n]` panics or reads OOB.

title: code_base + offset can wrap on high bases
description: `base + i as u64 + 5` and `next_ip.wrapping_add_signed` silently wrap when `code_base` is near u64::MAX, producing bogus xref source/target addresses without diagnostics.

title: Linear scan re-decodes displacement bytes as opcodes
description: `extract_code_to_code` always advances `i += 1` even after matching a 5-byte E8/E9, so disp32 bytes (which can legally be 0xE8/0xE9) generate spurious phantom call/jump xrefs.

title: Abstract virtual detection only flags null slots
description: `is_abstract: fn_addr == 0` misses MSVC `_purecall`/Itanium `__cxa_pure_virtual` stubs whose addresses are non-zero, mislabelling pure virtuals as concrete.

title: is_likely_tail_call accepts sites past function end
description: The check is `site <= function_end` with no lower bound and no membership test against the function's range, so any JMP anywhere below `function_end` to a known function is flagged as a tail call.

title: apply_fixups subtracts base from fixup.offset without bounds check
description: If fixup.offset < base this panics in debug or wraps to huge usize in release silently dropping fixups.

title: Default analyze_call_site caps register args at 4
description: `.min(4)` clamps reg-arg count even for SysV (6 regs) / AAPCS64 (8 regs), producing wrong call-site analysis.

title: AAPCS32 float arg name is literal "sN" instead of actual register
description: Returned ArgLocation always has name "sN" instead of "s0".."s15", breaking downstream consumers that key on register name.

title: aapcs64_ninth_arg_is_stack uses bare matches! without assert
description: `matches!(...)` returns bool that is discarded, so the test never actually verifies the location is on the stack.

title: PE lfanew bounds check `lfanew + 6 <= buf.len()` can overflow on 32-bit
description: Untrusted u32 lfanew cast to usize then added to 6 can wrap on 32-bit targets, bypassing the bound check and panicking on the subsequent slice.

title: Mach-O probe unwraps buf[0..4].try_into() with only a 4-byte minimum
description: Reachable code path; if some earlier change relaxes the len<4 guard, the unwrap panics—use unwrap_or like the sibling lines for consistency/defense-in-depth.

title: SBC binary mode underflows u16 in debug
description: `state.a as u16 - v as u16 - borrow` panics in debug builds whenever a < v+borrow (the common borrow case), corrupting all SBC semantics.

title: BRL target masks away PBR bits incorrectly
description: `& 0xFFFFFF` is applied after using full 64-bit next_addr, but the result is cast to u32 const without preserving the program bank, producing wrong long-branch targets when addr has bank bits.

title: ADC BCD overflow flag computed from wrong bin_result
description: `a ^ bin_result as u8` truncates the 9-bit `bin_result` before XOR, so the V flag is wrong whenever the binary sum produces carry, mis-detecting signed overflow.

title: Direct-page address adds 8-bit Const8 instead of widening
description: `E::add(E::reg(IL_REG_D), E::Const8(op1))` treats op1 as 8-bit, but 65816 direct-page math is 16-bit; downstream analysis sees a truncated operand.

title: SBC binary mode underflows u16 in debug builds
description: `state.a as u16 - v as u16 - borrow` panics whenever a < v+borrow (typical borrow path), making any debug-build SBC with a<v crash.

title: Branch target cast next_pc as i16 wraps for high PCs
description: Casting u16 next_pc to i16 then adding offset overflows for PC>=0x8000 in debug and produces wrong targets in release; should use i32 like the 65816 branch path.

title: BRL ignores program bank when computing target
description: next_addr is a u64 that includes bank bits, but the result is masked to 24 bits and stored without preserving PBR semantics, giving wrong long-branch destinations across banks.

title: ADC BCD overflow flag XORs truncated bin_result
description: `a ^ bin_result as u8` truncates the 9-bit sum to 8 bits before the V-flag XOR, so overflow is mis-detected whenever the binary add carried out of bit 7.

title: IndirectY zero-page high byte read without page wrap
description: `E::mem16(E::Const8(op1))` issues a 16-bit load, but on 6502 the high byte must wrap inside zero page (op1+1 mod 256); the IL model loses that wrap and downstream emulation gets wrong addresses.

title: FBcc displacement zero-extended and reads wrong bytes
description: `i32::from_be_bytes([0, 0, ext[2], ext[3]])` zero-extends instead of sign-extending and skips the high half of the 32-bit displacement, producing wrong branch targets for negative or long FPU branches.

title: FBcc target computed without including high displacement word
description: Only ext[2..4] is used so 32-bit FBcc displacements lose their upper 16 bits, breaking far branches.

title: EA mode 6 brief extension index register field uses 3 bits instead of 4
description: `(brief >> 4) & 7` masks off the D/A selector's neighbor and misidentifies register numbers >=8 on 68020 full-format extensions.

title: EXT mask 0xFEB8 mismatches 68k encoding
description: The correct EXT mask is 0xFFB8/0x4880; the looser 0xFEB8 will match unrelated opcodes like ADDA/SUBA with similar patterns and mis-decode them as EXT.

title: MOVEQ formats negative immediate as unsigned byte
description: `data.to_ne_bytes()[0]` loses the sign so `MOVEQ #-1,Dn` displays as `#$FF` rather than a sign-extended 32-bit constant.

title: ARM disassembler ignores configured big-endian mode
description: Uses `from_le_bytes` unconditionally to read the instruction word even though `ArmArch.little_endian` can be false and `endian()` returns `Endian::Big`, so big-endian binaries decode to garbage.

title: Thumb disassembler hard-codes little-endian halfword read
description: `u16::from_le_bytes` is used regardless of `little_endian`, producing wrong mnemonics on BE-8 Thumb code.

title: Wrong mask for Thumb-2 DP-modimm S bit
description: `(hw1 >> 4) & 0x10 != 0` actually tests bit 8 of `hw1` instead of bit 4 (the S flag), so the `s` suffix is reported for the wrong instructions and missed for the right ones.

title: BX rN lifted as Branch with target 0
description: For indirect BX where Rm != 14 the lifter returns `V7LiftOp::Branch(0)` instead of marking it indirect, fabricating a bogus jump target at address 0.

title: aarch64_system module missing from lib.rs
description: File src/aarch64_system.rs exists but is never declared with `pub mod aarch64_system;` so the entire system register analysis is dead code and unreachable.

title: Inverted is_store flag in SVE load/store decode
description: Variable `is_store = (word >> 21) & 1 == 0` is true when bit21=0, but ARM SVE encodings use bit21=0 for *loads* not stores, so load/store opcodes are swapped.

title: Dead match arm in SVE arithmetic decode
description: `(0, 0, _) => Add` is immediately shadowed by `(0, _, _) => Add` on the next line; the first pattern is unreachable and the immediate vs vector ADD/SUB distinction promised in the comment is never made.

title: SVE group filter accepts wrong encoding range
description: Comment claims SVE uses bits[28:25]=0100..0111 but architectural SVE base instructions use 0010; the `(4..=7).contains(&group)` check therefore misclassifies non-SVE NEON-adjacent words as SVE.

title: decode_all uses non-wrapping base+offset
description: `base + (i as u64) * 4` panics in debug if base is near u64::MAX; should use `wrapping_add` like the linear disassembler does in lib.rs:486.

title: RET uses pushed word-address as byte-address
description: RCALL/CALL push `(pc+2)/2` (word address) but RET sets `self.pc = addr` treating it as a byte address, so returns jump to half the correct PC.

title: service_interrupt pushes byte PC instead of word PC
description: Hardware pushes the word-address return PC but code pushes `self.pc as u16` (byte PC truncated), so RETI returns to the wrong address and is inconsistent with RCALL/CALL.

title: Timer0 TOV0 flag only set when TCNT0 ends at 0
description: Overflow flag is only raised when post-add tcnt0==0, missing every overflow that lands on any other value (e.g. add 300 cycles lands at non-zero).

title: load_flash panics when base > FLASH_SIZE
description: `end - base` underflows when `base > FLASH_SIZE` because `end` is clamped to FLASH_SIZE while base isn't, causing a panic in library code.

title: LDS/STS reads flash without bounds check
description: `self.flash[pc as usize + 2/3]` panics when PC is near the end of the 128 KiB flash region (no wrap-mask like fetch_word uses).

title: SUBI/SUB/CPI omit the SREG H (half-carry) flag
description: Half-carry is part of the AVR SREG spec for these instructions but the implementation never updates SREG_H, breaking BRHS/BRHC behavior after subtraction.

title: RET reads pushed word-address as byte PC
description: RCALL/CALL push `(pc+next)/2` (word address) but RET/RETI set `self.pc = popped` as a byte address, so every return jumps to half the intended target.

title: service_interrupt pushes byte PC instead of word PC
description: Hardware and the rest of this code push word-PC, but here `self.pc as u16` is the byte PC, making RETI inconsistent with RCALL/CALL and returning to the wrong address.

title: Timer0 TOV0 only fires when TCNT0 lands on zero
description: Overflow flag is gated by `self.tcnt0 == 0` after the add, so any tick whose cycle delta wraps past 256 but doesn't land on zero silently loses the overflow.

title: load_flash panics when base exceeds FLASH_SIZE
description: `end` is clamped to FLASH_SIZE while `base` is not, so `end - base` underflows and panics for any caller passing an out-of-range base.

title: LDS/STS reads flash[pc+2/+3] without bounds or wrap
description: Unlike fetch_word, these direct indexes panic when PC is near the top of the 128 KiB flash array (e.g. last word executes LDS).

title: SUBI/SUB/CPI never update SREG H (half-carry)
description: The AVR spec requires H for these subs, but the implementation only computes C/V/N/Z/S, so BRHS/BRHC after a subtract will misbehave.

title: wide_imm sign-extension corruption
description: `i64::from(imm) | (i64::from(imm_hi) << 32)` sign-extends a negative low 32-bit imm into the high bits before OR, corrupting the 64-bit immediate for LDDW.

title: parse_insns ignores 16-byte LDDW
description: Iterating in fixed 8-byte chunks treats the second half of BPF_LD_DW_IMM as a separate instruction, mis-decoding the program and shifting all subsequent analysis.

title: trace raw word sign-extends imm
description: `(insn.imm as u64) << 32` sign-extends a negative i32 to u64, overwriting the lower fields via OR and producing wrong raw instruction words.

title: visited set keyed on PC only
description: Marking PC as visited regardless of incoming state means alternate paths/states at the same PC are silently dropped, masking real verifier errors and producing unsound 'safe' results.

title: Jmp32 class not excluded from uninit check
description: The early-out only skips class 0x05 (Jmp) but not 0x06 (Jmp32), so Jmp32 instructions fall through into load/store checks that don't apply.

title: MethodHeader::decode accepts garbage as Fat header without checking flag bits
description: after rejecting tiny via `first & 0x03 == 0b10`, code proceeds to Fat parsing without verifying `first & 0x03 == 0x03`, so any non-tiny byte is silently treated as a fat header.

title: switch decode multiplies attacker-controlled u32 count by 4 in usize without checked_mul
description: `let total = 5 + n * 4` where `n` comes from raw bytes; on 32-bit targets `n * 4` can wrap and bypass the subsequent `need(bytes, total)` check.

title: StreamHeader::parse scans the entire remaining buffer for a NUL terminator
description: `remaining.iter().position` has no name-length cap, so a missing NUL inside a header makes it greedily consume unrelated downstream bytes.

title: decode_compressed_uint returns Truncated for invalid prefix bytes
description: leading bytes with the top three bits `111` are an invalid encoding, not a truncation; callers cannot distinguish malformed blobs from short input.

title: MethodHeader::decode accepts arbitrary bytes as a Fat header
description: after the tiny-flag check fails, the code parses a Fat header without verifying `first & 0x03 == 0x03`, so garbage or another section type is silently treated as a valid method header.

title: switch instruction computes `5 + n * 4` without checked arithmetic
description: `n` is a u32 read from input cast to usize; on 32-bit targets the multiplication can wrap and bypass the later `need(bytes, total)` bounds check.

title: StreamHeader::parse has no upper bound on the name scan
description: `remaining.iter().position(|&b| b == 0)` walks the rest of the metadata buffer if a header is missing its NUL, so malformed input causes the parser to consume downstream stream headers as a name.

title: decode_compressed_uint reports invalid prefixes as `Truncated`
description: input bytes with the top three bits `111` are not a valid ECMA-335 compressed-integer prefix; returning `Truncated` conflates malformed encodings with short input.

title: StackDepthAnalysis::analyze adds deltas with unchecked i32 arithmetic
description: `depth += delta` is plain wrapping/overflowing addition in release; carefully chosen deltas can wrap past the `depth < 0` and `depth > 1024` guards.

title: conditional fall-through leader only added when branches exist
description: The fall-through leader insert is nested inside `for bi in arch.get_branches(instr)`, so conditional instructions whose branches list is empty never register the fall-through as a leader, producing wrong CFG splits.

title: parse_chunk_header misreads Lua 5.4 header
description: For 5.4 the byte at offset 5 is the format byte (0), not an endian flag, and offsets 6/7 belong to the LUAC_DATA signature — so endian/int_size/size_t_size are populated with the wrong bytes.

title: TEST/TESTSET not flagged BRANCH in lua54_fmt
description: `lua54_fmt` only marks ops 55..=63 as TestJump; TEST(64)/TESTSET(65) fall into Abc with InstrFlags::NONE, so they are not treated as conditional branches despite is_branch_opcode listing them.

title: signed offset * 4 may panic on overflow
description: `off as u64 * 4` on a negative i64 cast to u64 yields a huge value; the bare `*` (not wrapping_mul) can overflow and panic in debug builds.

title: make_iabc lacks operand bounds masking
description: `a`, `b`, `c`, `k` are shifted directly without masking to their bit widths, so out-of-range callers silently corrupt adjacent fields (k or neighbouring operands) instead of erroring.

title: jump_targets cast to usize can wrap on negative target
description: `(i as i64 + 1 + sj as i64) as usize` silently wraps to an enormous usize when the computed PC is negative, producing bogus jump targets instead of being filtered.

title: INS msb computation underflow
description: `rd as u32 - shamt + 1` panics in debug when malformed input has rd<shamt, since both come from raw 5-bit fields with no validation.

title: decode_word slices raw[..4] without bounds check
description: `raw[..4].to_vec()` panics if a caller passes a slice shorter than 4 bytes, since the function takes a precomputed `word` separate from `raw`.

title: branch_target overflow at kseg0 addresses
description: `(pc as i32 + 4 + offset) as u32` panics in debug for high addresses like 0x80000000 where pc-as-i32 is INT_MIN and negative offsets overflow.

title: scan_mips_strings unwrap on None run_start
description: When `min_len==0` and a non-printable byte appears before any printable byte, `buf.len() >= min_len` is true but `run_start` is None, so `run_start.unwrap()` panics.

title: Lwc1/Ldc1 lose FP bit pattern via f32->f64 cast
description: Storing loaded 32-bit FP value as `f32::from_bits(bits) as f64` canonicalizes NaNs and loses exact bit pattern; should preserve raw bits in the FPR.

title: FPU load/store hardcoded little-endian
description: Lwc1/Ldc1/Swc1/Sdc1 always assemble bytes LSB-first, ignoring MipsEndian, so big-endian MIPS programs decode FP loads/stores incorrectly.

title: alu_xor sets wrong carry flag
description: MSP430 spec requires C = NOT(result==0), but code uses `src & 0x8000`, producing incorrect Carry for XOR.

title: write_operand silently drops memory writes
description: Indexed/Absolute/Indirect destinations fall through without writing, so RRC/RRA/SXT/SWPB on memory operands corrupt nothing but lose the result.

title: Msp430State::load truncates index to u16
description: `addr.wrapping_add(i as u16)` silently wraps for data.len() > 65536 - addr, overwriting earlier bytes without error.

title: alu_xor sets carry from src sign bit instead of NOT Zero
description: MSP430 spec defines XOR C-flag as `result != 0`, but code uses `src & 0x8000`, yielding wrong Carry for XOR/INV emulated instructions.

title: write_operand silently drops Indexed/Absolute/Indirect writes
description: For RRC/RRA/SXT/SWPB targeting memory, the write-back paths are empty stubs, so emulated results are never stored — silent data loss.

title: Msp430State::load uses `addr.wrapping_add(i as u16)`
description: Loading a slice larger than 65536-addr silently wraps the index and overwrites already-written bytes instead of erroring or stopping at the address-space end.

title: FlatMemory::load uses `addr.wrapping_add(i as u16)`
description: Same wrap-around index bug duplicated; loads >64 KiB silently smash earlier memory without bounds check.

title: BCLRL incorrectly flagged as RET
description: BCLRL (xo=16, LK=1) is a call-via-LR but it returns `InstrFlags::RET`, so callers treat function calls as returns.

title: BCCTRL flagged as BRANCH instead of CALL
description: When LK bit is set (BCCTRL), the flags should include CALL but the code always uses BRANCH|INDIRECT, breaking indirect-call analysis.

title: Absolute branch target not sign-extended on PPC64
description: `u64::from(u32::from_ne_bytes(offset.to_ne_bytes()))` zero-extends the 32-bit signed offset to u64, producing wrong absolute targets for negative addresses on 64-bit PPC.

title: Address+offset cast may truncate on 32-bit hosts
description: `self.base + self.offset as u64` is fine, but `addr + self.offset as u64` lacks wrap check; in extreme cases could wrap silently.

title: Branch target parsing stops at non-hex but accepts partial
description: `u64::from_str_radix(&hex, 16)` succeeds on any prefix of hex chars from operands like "$ABCD,..." misclassifying targets when operand format changes.

title: BCLRL incorrectly flagged as RET
description: BCLRL (LK=1) is a call through LR, not a return, but both BCLR and BCLRL get InstrFlags::RET causing CFG to terminate at calls.

title: BCCTRL flagged as BRANCH not CALL
description: When LK=1 the instruction is a call via CTR; code unconditionally sets BRANCH|INDIRECT so callgraph misses these calls.

title: Absolute branch target zero-extended on PPC64
description: u64::from(u32 bit-pattern) loses sign extension; negative absolute targets become low-4GB addresses instead of sign-extended 64-bit addresses.

title: RFI returns RET for both xo=18 and xo=50
description: xo=50 is rfid (64-bit return-from-interrupt) on real PPC but xo=18 is rfi; conflating them as same mnemonic loses 64-bit context (and 50 actually overlaps STDX-like decoding concerns).

title: Linear disassembler advances 4 on any error even with <4 bytes left
description: If bytes.len()-offset is 1..3, error path increments offset by 4 producing a final Err item, harmless but yields a spurious "truncated" error per tail.

title: c.fld uses wrong base register
description: Uses `xr(rs2_prime + 8)` as address base (rs2_prime is already +8, becoming x16-x23) instead of `xr(rs1_prime)`, producing wrong disassembly for every c.fld.

title: c.addi4spn nzuimm samples wrong bits
description: `(hw >> 2) & 0xFF` reads hw[9:2] but the nzuimm field is hw[12:5]; the decoder drops hw[10:11] (nzuimm[5:4]) and produces incorrect immediates.

title: c.lw immediate decoded from wrong bits
description: `imm6 = (hw>>2)&0x7` samples hw[4:2] (rs2' field) instead of hw[6:5] (imm[6,2]); every c.lw/c.sw offset is wrong.

title: disassemble rejects 16-bit compressed instructions
description: Returns error when bytes.len()<4 even though C-extension half-words (low 2 bits != 0b11) are legal 2-byte instructions, so compressed code at end-of-buffer fails.

title: branch target sign-extension via i32-to-u64 cast
description: `address.0.wrapping_add(offset as u64)` casts i32 to u64 without sign extension to i64 first, so negative branch offsets wrap to a huge positive value on 64-bit targets.

title: CALL displacement sign-extension wrong
description: `((instr & 0x3FFF_FFFF) as i32) << 2` masks the sign bit before shifting, so negative 30-bit displacements (high bit set) are treated as positive, breaking backward calls.

title: SLL/SRL/SRA opcodes wrong
description: Format-3 shift op3 codes are 0x25/0x26/0x27 in SPARC v8, but the emulator uses 0x0D/0x0E/0x0F which collide with UMUL/UDIV/SDIV, so shifts never execute and mul/div mis-execute as shifts.

title: Half/word loads can overflow address arithmetic
description: `addr + 1`, `addr + 2`, `addr + 3` use checked add on u32 and will panic in debug when `addr == u32::MAX` or near it; should use `wrapping_add` like elsewhere.

title: LDUH/LD ignore alignment
description: SPARC requires halfword/word loads to be aligned and raise MemoryAddressNotAligned, but `exec_fmt3` performs the access unconditionally with no alignment check.

title: SparcMemory::load is O(n) per byte
description: `load()` looks up the page hash map for every byte, calling `entry`+`get_mut` per iteration instead of batching by page, making large loads dramatically slower than necessary.

title: br_table label count untrusted allocation
description: count is derived from attacker-controlled ULEB128 and used as `Vec::with_capacity(count + 1)` with `0..=count` loop, causing huge allocation or panic in debug when uleb saturates to usize::MAX.

title: SLEB128 left-shift overflow
description: `i64::from(b & 0x7f) << shift` panics in debug when shift==63 and bit 0x40 (or higher) is set in the byte before the overflow check on line 71 fires.

title: ULEB128 high-bit accepted at shift 63
description: `u64::from(b & 0x7f) << shift` at shift==63 silently truncates bits 7..63 of the final byte without rejecting non-canonical encodings, accepting malformed LEB128.

title: disassemble may slice past returned size
description: `bytes[..size.min(bytes.len())]` masks decoder bugs by silently truncating instead of erroring, hiding inconsistencies where `decode_wasm` returns size > bytes.len().

title: classify_branch hardcodes is_64bit=true
description: In 32-bit code 0x40-0x4F are INC/DEC, not REX, so they get skipped as prefixes and the following byte is misclassified as the opcode.

title: disp32 absolute reported as RipRelative in 32-bit mode
description: EffectiveAddr::decode returns RipRelative for mod=0/rm=5 in 32-bit, but that encoding is absolute disp32, not RIP-relative, misleading downstream analysis.

title: EVEX map field masked with 0x07 includes reserved bit
description: EVEX P0 has mm at bits [1:0] with bit 2 reserved/zero; using `p0 & 0x07` lets a stray reserved bit corrupt the VexMap selection.

title: EvexPrefix.b_prime decoded from a reserved bit
description: Standard EVEX P0 bit 3 is reserved (must be 0); treating it as B' produces a phantom register-extension flag that callers may use to fabricate r16-r31 indices.

title: VEX/EVEX tail length ignores imm8 for many opcodes
description: decode_vex_tail always passes imm=0, so VPSHUFD/VCMPSS/etc. under-measure by 1 byte and silently desync the streaming length decoder.

title: Far-pointer length uses operand-size immz instead of fixed offset
description: 0xEA/0x9A is ptr16:16 or ptr16:32 whose offset width follows operand size; using ctx.immz is correct for 16/32 but the comment claiming "operand-size + 2-byte selector" together with no 64-bit-mode guard mis-handles the 64-bit invalid case as a valid 6-byte length.

title: extract_hex_target misparses conditional branch operands
description: trim_start_matches('$') skips nothing when operands start with cond like "C,$1234" and take_while hex-digit will consume the 'C' (a valid hex digit) returning 0xC instead of the real target, so JR C / JP C / CALL C call_targets and branch_targets are wrong.

title: opcode_cycles default arm returns 4 for prefix opcodes
description: CB/DD/ED/FD (0xCB,0xDD,0xED,0xFD) fall through to the catch-all 4-cycle case, so total_cycles in analyze() under-counts every prefixed instruction by a large margin.

title: Z80Memory::load can underflow on empty bytes at boundary
description: when bytes is empty and start==0x10000 boundary cases or when start>end after clamping, end - start can underflow usize causing panic or wrong slice; no explicit guard that addr+len fits.

title: set_s uses bitand with literal true
description: `v & true` is a no-op masquerading as intent; harmless but indicates copy-paste error and obscures the actual sign-flag predicate.

title: length cast u64->usize truncates on 32-bit
description: `len as usize` silently truncates a user-supplied u64 length on 32-bit targets, producing a wrong scan window.

title: `f.read(&mut buf)` return value ignored, magic detected from possibly-uninitialized prefix
description: `read` may return fewer than 4 bytes; the match then uses whatever happens to be in `buf`, misdetecting format for tiny files.

title: `if let Ok(_) =` ignores the TcpStream and leaks it until drop; also racy status check
description: Using `if let Ok(_) =` instead of `.is_ok()` is a clippy lint and the open connection is dropped synchronously, but the daemon-status probe has no read handshake, so any listener (not just rustre-daemon) reports "running".

title: Unknown long flags silently become config overrides
description: `apply_long_kv` falls through to `args.overrides.insert` so a typo like `--quie=true` is silently accepted as a config key instead of being rejected as unknown.

title: Long-flag matcher accepts single-letter aliases
description: `--v`, `--V`, `--h`, `--q`, `--f`, `--c` are accepted as long flags, conflating GNU long-option convention and confusing users.

title: Tilde in default config path not expanded
description: `~/.rustre.cfg` is passed to `PathBuf::from` without `$HOME` expansion, so it only matches a literal `~` directory and never finds the user's home config.

title: `version` shorthand collides with `-v` verbose
description: positional `v` maps to `Version` while `-v` means verbose, so `rustre-cli v` prints version unexpectedly when user meant verbose toggle.

title: Unknown `--key=value` silently stored as config override
description: Typos in long flags bypass validation and inject arbitrary config keys instead of erroring, masking user mistakes.

title: Long-option parser accepts `--v`/`--h`/`--q`/`--V`/`--f`/`--c` as aliases
description: Conflates short/long flag conventions and allows ambiguous invocations.

title: Tilde not expanded in default config path search
description: `PathBuf::from("~/.rustre.cfg")` never resolves to the user's home directory, so the documented default location is unreachable.

title: Positional `v` maps to Version subcommand
description: Users typing `rustre-cli v <binary>` unexpectedly hit Version instead of getting a clear error or verbose flag.

title: Config loader allows duplicate keys silently
description: `values.insert` overwrites without warning, hiding shadowed configuration entries from the user.

title: read_patched returns zero for bytes outside patch
description: Bytes outside the patch range are filled with 0 instead of the underlying original/memory bytes, so the documented "blend" returns wrong data to callers.

title: apply_to_buf unchecked u64 add
description: buf_end = buf_base + buf.len() and p_end = p_start + len() use unchecked arithmetic; with high addresses these wrap and can skip patches or pass through the bounds guard, leading to incorrect copies or panics.

title: Memory::read wraps current_addr near u64::MAX
description: addr + read_bytes uses wrapping Address::add, so a near-MAX read can wrap to a low address that happens to lie in a segment, returning wrong bytes instead of SegmentFault.

title: align_down divides by user-supplied align
description: Although guarded by `align <= 1`, the modulo still executes for any `align` value; no panic for 0, but documented contract that any non-power-of-two yields odd results is not enforced and can mis-align addresses silently.

title: Shift overflow with Size::B16 in pretty_print
description: `1u64 << (size.bits() - 1)` becomes `1u64 << 127` which panics in debug and is UB-equivalent overflow for u64.

title: Shift overflow in apply_cast sign extension for B16
description: `1u64 << (bits - 1)` with bits=128 panics on shift-overflow when casting to a 16-byte int type.

title: MemoryProvider default reads index without length check
description: `read_u8/u16/u32/u64` index `b[0..N]` after `read_bytes` which may return a shorter Vec, causing an out-of-bounds panic in library code.

title: Parser::advance panics on empty token stream
description: `&self.tokens[self.pos]` indexes before the bounds check, so an empty token vector triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of returning Eof.

title: Pointer arithmetic uses unchecked add/sub/mul
description: `lu + ru * ptr_stride` and `lu - ru * ptr_stride` are plain u64 ops with no wrapping/checked variants, panicking on overflow in debug builds for large pointers or indices.

title: Shl does not mask shift amount but Shr does
description: `lu.wrapping_shl(ru as u32)` truncates ru to u32 and relies on wrapping_shl masking, while Shr masks with `& 63` — inconsistent semantics and `ru as u32` truncation hides large shift bugs.

title: read_memory base+len u64 overflow in range check
description: `base + page.len() as u64` can wrap for pages mapped near u64::MAX, causing the bounds check to incorrectly accept or reject addresses.

title: scan_memory_pattern address arithmetic can overflow
description: `base + offset as u64` is unchecked and can wrap for pages mapped at the top of the address space, producing bogus match addresses.

title: write_memory to unmapped address inserts page at raw addr unaligned
description: When no page contains the address, a new page is inserted keyed by `raw`, which can overlap/shadow existing pages and makes subsequent reads order-dependent on HashMap iteration.

title: single_step increments rip by 1 byte
description: x86 instructions are variable-length; advancing rip by exactly 1 doesn't model any real instruction and will confuse consumers expecting realistic stepping.

title: timestamp u128→u64 lossy cast
description: `d.as_millis() as u64` silently truncates a u128 millisecond count without checked conversion.

title: read_byte uses Vec::pop() (LIFO) for a byte queue
description: pop() returns the last pushed byte, so any buffered bytes are replayed in reverse order, corrupting packet framing.

title: ChecksumMismatch fields swapped
description: The error reports `expected: computed` and `got: expected`, inverting the two values shown to callers.

title: escape() casts raw byte to char producing multi-byte UTF-8
description: Bytes >0x7F are pushed as `char` into a String, expanding to 2-byte UTF-8 sequences and breaking RSP framing/checksum for binary payloads.

title: parse_vfile_open cannot parse negative errno responses
description: `i32::from_str_radix` rejects the leading '-' in `F-1,errno`, silently dropping all error replies as None.

title: set_thread treats empty reply as success
description: An empty RSP response means "unsupported" but the code accepts it as OK, hiding stub capability gaps.

title: new_data panics on oversize payload
description: Library function uses .expect() on u16::try_from, crashing process when data.len() > 65535 instead of returning Result.

title: Packet ID not advanced after connect reset
description: connect() pushes a Reset packet with next_id but doesn't toggle it, so first send() reuses the same id, breaking sequence-number protocol.

title: build_read_virtual_memory header layout mismatches parser
description: Builder writes target_addr at offset 8, but KdManipulateState parser treats offset 8..12 as return_status (HEADER_SIZE=12), so build/parse are inconsistent.

title: HEADER_SIZE 12 contradicts doc comment "8-byte header"
description: payload field doc says "after the 8-byte header" but HEADER_SIZE=12 is used to slice payload, causing 4 bytes of real data to be discarded.

title: byte_count cast to usize without validation
description: On 16-bit-clean input it's fine, but combined with no upper bound check vs raw.len() before slicing — slice is then checked, OK; however total = HEADER_SIZE + byte_count can be used unchecked elsewhere via parse_recv loop allowing memory growth.

title: parse_recv resync skips 1 byte after failed packet
description: When KdPacket::from_bytes fails due to unknown type code, cursor advances by 1, but byte_count of failed packet is ignored, causing potential reparse of payload as headers and CPU waste.

title: new_data panics on oversize payload
description: Library uses .expect() on u16::try_from so data.len() > 65535 crashes the process instead of returning an error.

title: connect() reuses next_id without advancing
description: Reset packet is queued with self.next_id but the counter is never toggled, so the first subsequent send() emits a packet with the same id, breaking KD sequence numbering.

title: build_read_virtual_memory layout inconsistent with parser
description: Builder places target_addr at bytes 8..16, but KdManipulateState::from_bytes treats bytes 8..12 as return_status (HEADER_SIZE=12), so round-tripping a built request mis-decodes the address.

title: payload doc says "after 8-byte header" but code uses 12
description: Doc comment and HEADER_SIZE disagree; consumers relying on the 8-byte assumption will mis-index the payload.

title: parse_recv resync advances only 1 byte on failure
description: On a malformed/unknown type, the loop advances 1 byte and re-reads byte_count from payload bytes, potentially looping over the entire buffer for each garbage packet (O(n*pkt) CPU).

title: PT_LOAD end address can overflow u64
description: `p_vaddr + size` is unchecked addition that panics in debug or wraps in release when a malicious core file specifies large vaddr+filesz.

title: wifsignaled cast to i8 truncates and mis-detects signaled status
description: `((status & 0x7f) + 1) as i8 >= 2` truncates a 32-bit value to i8 producing wrong results for valid signaled statuses; correct macro is `((signed)((status & 0x7f) + 1) >> 1) > 0`.

title: pr_sid parsed from wrong offset with arbitrary wrapping_sub(16)
description: `pr_sid` is read at offset 28 (which is actually inside pr_fname) and then `wrapping_sub(16)` is applied with comment "approximate", yielding garbage session IDs.

title: NT_FILE path_end+1 can index past data.len()
description: When the final filename has no NUL terminator, `path_end == data.len()` and `name_ptr = path_end + 1` then the next iteration's slice `data[name_ptr..]` panics with out-of-bounds.

title: read bounds check uses unchecked addition
description: `addr + len as u64` in PtraceMemoryOps::read can wrap to a small value when addr is near u64::MAX, bypassing the mapped-region check; same pattern in write at line 664.

title: ExceptionType::as_mask shift overflow
description: `1 << self.to_raw()` panics in debug / produces wrong mask when Unknown(n) carries n>=32 from from_raw.

title: ARM64 breakpoint fallback corrupts original bytes
description: When the 4-byte original cannot be read, falls back to `[original[0],0,0,0]` so `remove_breakpoint` writes three zero bytes over real code.

title: read offset+size can overflow usize
description: `offset + size > backing.len()` is computed without checked_add; on huge size this wraps and bypasses the bounds check, enabling out-of-bounds slice panic.

title: read_memory address+size addition can wrap
description: `addr + size as u64` and `base + page.len() as u64` are unchecked, so a near-u64::MAX addr wraps and matches an unrelated page.

title: find_region_mut uses unchecked add
description: `r.address + r.size` can overflow whereas the immutable sibling uses `end()` via saturating_add, giving inconsistent behavior at the top of the address space.

title: attach never sets running flag
description: attach() takes &self and only records pid in session but never sets running=true, so emulate() will always fail with "emulator not started" in production use (only tests work by mutating the field directly).

title: map_memory overlap check can overflow
description: `addr + size` and `region.addr + region.size` are unchecked u64 adds that wrap on near-u64::MAX inputs, defeating the overlap check and allowing aliased mappings.

title: emulate PC increment can overflow and skip until
description: `self.pc += stride` panics on overflow in debug; also if `until` is not stride-aligned the PC steps past it and never matches, wasting up to max_steps iterations.

title: write_memory_direct length math can wrap
description: `addr + data.len() as u64` is unchecked and `data.len() as u64` casts usize without overflow check, so a crafted large slice can wrap and pass the bounds check, writing out of region.

title: v2 emulate infinite-loops on misaligned end
description: `while pc != end` with stride 4 will overshoot a non-4-aligned `end` and spin until max_insn=10000, returning a misleading exit_addr instead of an error.

title: end_address can overflow
description: `self.address + self.size` is an unchecked add used in overlaps/contains_addr, so regions near u64::MAX produce wrong end and break overlap detection.

title: Command-line built without quoting allows argument injection
description: `opts.args` are concatenated into the `CreateProcessW` command line separated by spaces with no escaping or quoting, so an arg containing spaces, quotes, or `&` is misparsed or can inject extra commands.

title: CriticalSection parsed with x64 offsets unconditionally
description: Field offsets 0x10/0x18/0x20 are the 64-bit RTL_CRITICAL_SECTION layout; for WoW64/32-bit targets the struct is smaller (0x08/0x0C/0x10), producing wrong owning-thread and semaphore values.

title: FormatMessageW length used without clamping to buffer
description: `buf[..len as usize]` will panic if `FormatMessageW` ever returns a length greater than the 512-element buffer (or via an unexpected return convention).

title: walk_heap can emit entries that overrun the buffer
