description: Loop `for i in 0..len as u64 { let a = addr + i; }` wraps/panics when addr+len exceeds u64::MAX, allowing fuzz-controlled len to crash the sanitizer.

title: f64 silently truncated to f32 in MySQL Real param
description: `GraphParam::Real(f) => mysql::Value::Float(f as f32)` discards precision and overflows to inf for large finite f64 values when binding parameters.

title: MySQL last_insert_id u64→i64 cast can wrap
description: `result.last_insert_id().unwrap_or(0) as i64` silently produces a negative id for AUTO_INCREMENT values above i64::MAX.

title: Corrupted node properties JSON silently dropped
description: `serde_json::from_str(&props_str).unwrap_or_default()` returns an empty map on parse failure, hiding DB corruption from callers reading nodes.

title: Corrupted edge properties JSON silently dropped
description: Same `unwrap_or_default()` pattern in `row_to_edge` discards real data on bad JSON instead of erroring.

title: now_unix returns 0 if clock is before UNIX_EPOCH
description: `duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap_or(Duration::ZERO)` yields timestamp 0 silently if the system clock is skewed, corrupting created_at/updated_at.

title: list_backups does not filter to files
description: `read_dir` results include any directory named `graph_backup_*`, which callers may then try to read as a JSON backup file.

title: select(start,end) produces wrong selection for empty/zero range
description: `e.saturating_sub(1)` makes select(0,0) yield a 1-byte selection at offset 0 instead of an empty selection.

title: read_exact `offset+len` can overflow usize
description: Adding attacker-controlled `offset` and `len` without checked_add can wrap and bypass the bounds check on 32-bit targets or with huge inputs.

title: annotations_overlapping `offset+len` and `a.offset+a.size` can overflow
description: Unchecked additions can panic in debug or wrap silently in release, returning wrong overlap set.

title: find_hex_pattern slices token at byte index 1 without UTF-8 boundary check
description: `&t[..1]` panics when the token's first char is multi-byte UTF-8 (e.g. user pastes a non-ASCII char), turning a parse error into a panic.

title: search_with_captures slice OOB panic
description: abs_start can exceed data.len() when cap.start > pattern length, causing `data[abs_start..abs_end]` to panic since only abs_end is clamped.

title: offset+bytes.len() can wrap on 32-bit/huge offset
description: `offset + self.bytes.len()` is unchecked addition; a caller-supplied huge offset overflows usize and bypasses the bounds check.

title: SQL LIKE wildcard injection in search_by_name
description: user input is wrapped with `%{name}%` without escaping `%`/`_`/`\`, letting callers match unintended rows or cause expensive scans (same at :1069 and :1211).

title: read_u16le/read_u32le bounds check can overflow
description: `off + 2 > self.data.len()` and `off + 4 > self.data.len()` perform unchecked usize add; a huge off (from negative i64 cast) wraps and bypasses the check, then `self.data[off..off+4]` panics.

title: Shl/Shr cast i64 shift count to u32
description: `b as u32` silently truncates negative or large shift amounts before wrapping_shl/shr, producing surprising results for the user pattern language.

title: local variable initializer dropped when spaces surround `=`
description: splitn(3,' ') on `int i = 5` puts ` = 5` in parts[2] which is ignored, so `local int i = 5;` parses with value=None.

title: Assert message containing comma is truncated
description: `split_once(',')` splits at first comma so any condition/message with a comma loses content.

title: author filter case-sensitivity mismatch
description: `TemplateSearch.author` is stored verbatim (no lowercasing setter) but compared against lowercased entry.author, so any uppercase query never matches.

title: Printf args silently dropped
description: Parser never extracts arguments after the format string; `Printf("x=%d", v)` stores empty args, breaking formatting downstream.

title: array count parse failure silently defaults to 1
description: `count_str.parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(1)` masks malformed array sizes like `arr[N]` instead of returning a Parse error.

title: `offset as usize + size` may overflow before bounds check on 32-bit
description: Computing `end` before comparing to `data.len()` can wrap when offset is near usize::MAX on 32-bit targets, bypassing the EOD check.

title: Annotation::range can overflow
description: `self.offset + self.len` is not checked and panics in debug if offset+len exceeds usize::MAX.

title: Annotation iteration unbounded
description: `for i in ann.offset..ann.offset+ann.len` iterates the full annotation range every render, so a large `len` causes a render-time hang/DoS.

title: ensure_cursor_visible underflow when visible_rows=0
description: If `config.visible_rows == 0`, `cursor_row - visible_rows + 1` and `top_row + 0` make the `>=` branch trigger and subtract underflows (no `.max(1)` like elsewhere).

title: DiffHighlightMap offset+len overflow
description: `region.offset + region.len` and `region.offset + i` are unchecked and can overflow with crafted DiffRegion input; OnlyInLeft branch also lacks a left-buffer bounds check (unlike OnlyInRight).

title: selected_bytes panics if sel.start>sel.end
description: `selected_bytes` only clamps `sel.end` to buffer len but never validates `sel.start <= sel.end`, so an inverted selection panics on slice.

title: Division overflow panic in const fold
description: `x / y` panics when x=i64::MIN and y=-1 (signed division overflow).

title: Modulo overflow panic in const fold
description: `x % y` panics when x=i64::MIN and y=-1 (signed remainder overflow).

title: Unreachable duplicate Add match arm
description: `HlilExpr::Add(a,b)` is matched twice (lines 349 and 434); the second arm is dead code masking intent.

title: Sign flag hardcoded to 64-bit width
description: `set_arith_flags` always passes `64` to `set_sign_flag`, so SF for 8/16/32-bit ops is taken from bit 63 instead of the operand MSB.

title: wide_high u32 add can overflow
description: `n + 1` on a parsed `u32` panics in debug / wraps in release if the source token is `v4294967295`.

title: ROL count mod uses operand width but x86 masks by 5/6 bits
description: `arg(1) % w` differs from CPU which first masks count to 5 (or 6 for 64-bit) and then mods, producing wrong CF for shift counts >=32 on 8/16-bit operands.

title: Non-wrapping add in Memory::write byte loop
description: `addr + i as u64` can panic in debug on overflow while the symmetric `read` uses `wrapping_add`, causing inconsistent crash behavior on high-address writes.

title: alloc_addr increments without overflow check
description: `self.next_addr += 4` will panic in debug builds once next_addr nears u64::MAX, and silently wrap in release, producing duplicate synthetic addresses.

title: Unchecked `unwrap` on `block.instrs.last()`
description: `block.instrs.last().unwrap()` is only safe due to the prior `is_empty` continue, but is brittle and would panic if that guard were ever removed/refactored — should use `if let Some(..)`.

title: Length stored as u8 silently truncated into size: usize
description: `size: self.length as usize` copies the u8 length, but callers may expect `size` to reflect a larger byte size; the builder API only exposes `length(u8)` so any instruction >255 bytes is silently impossible.

title: Shl/Shr const-fold uses `b % bits` instead of saturating to 0
description: Shifts by >= width produce `x << 0 = x` instead of 0, contradicting safe_shl/safe_shr semantics in lib.rs and producing wrong constants.

title: Shift count cast `b as u32` truncates 64-bit value
description: A 64-bit shift amount whose low 32 bits are 0 but upper bits non-zero would underflow `% bits` to 0 after truncation, mis-folding shifts.

title: Trivial-PHI elimination only handles len==1
description: A PHI with multiple identical sources (the canonical trivial case per phi_placement::is_trivial) is never eliminated, leaving dead phis after SSA simplification.

title: Dominator entry assumed to be blocks[0] despite doc saying "lowest id"
description: If `func.blocks` is not sorted by id, the entry chosen disagrees with the documented contract and dominator results become wrong.

title: Shift mask is 127 instead of operand bit-width
description: Masking shift count with `& 127` allows shifts of 64..=127 on machine-sized values, which is undefined for the source ISA semantics and produces wrong constants for typical 32/64-bit IL operands.

title: PHI uses positional zip of preds and srcs
description: `eval_phi` zips `predecessors` with `srcs` by index, assuming the two vectors are kept in the same order; any reordering of `predecessors` (e.g. by `remove_dead_blocks` retain) silently maps PHI sources to the wrong predecessors.

title: `block`/`block_mut` panic on missing BB
description: Library APIs `expect("BasicBlock not found")` on a HashMap lookup, so malformed input (e.g. successor referencing a removed block, common after `remove_dead_blocks`) panics inside library code.

title: Mach-O byte-swapped magic reads cpu type little-endian
description: For magics `0xCEFA_EDFE` and `0xCFFA_EDFE` (byte-swapped Mach-O), the cpu field is read with `from_le_bytes` instead of `from_be_bytes`, yielding wrong arch detection.

title: Fat Mach-O slice offset/size never validated against data length
description: `off` and `sz` from each fat_arch entry are stored without checking `off + sz <= data.len()`, so later consumers can read out-of-range and downstream loaders panic.

title: CALL rel32 scan skips final valid offset
description: Loop bound `data.len().saturating_sub(5)` makes a 5-byte section iterate 0..0 (skipping i=0) and in general misses the last valid CALL site at index `len-5`.

title: AArch64 Call26 silently truncates out-of-range branch
description: `(delta/4) as i32` then masked to 26 bits has no range check, so far branches silently encode wrong target instead of returning `Truncation` error like x86 variants do.

title: PE entry-point sum `image_base + entry` can overflow u64
description: `image_base + entry` uses unchecked addition on attacker-controlled values; release builds wrap silently producing a bogus EP.

title: Untrusted count multiplied without check
description: `count` read from input is multiplied by `3 * 8` and used as allocation/length bound without checked arithmetic, causing usize overflow on hostile core files leading to bypassed bounds check.

title: Unbounded allocation from bloom_size
description: `Vec::with_capacity(bloom_size)` allocates based on attacker-controlled u32 from .gnu.hash before validating it against `data.len()`, enabling OOM.

title: offset + SIZE bounds check can wrap
description: `offset + Self::SIZE > data.len()` uses unchecked addition; a near-usize::MAX `offset` wraps and falsely passes the truncation check (same pattern in Chdr64::parse line 85).

title: sym_idx u32 increment can overflow
description: In `scan_all_symbols`, `sym_idx += 1` over a chain length attacker can control may overflow u32 (panics in debug builds) for crafted hash tables.

title: KN double constant flag bit not cleared before shift
description: `(kval << 32) | lo` leaves the integer-flag LSB in bit 32 of f64 bits, corrupting any KN double whose ULEB128 high-word LSB is set.

title: Unchecked u32 add of first_line+line
description: `first_line as u32 + line` can wrap silently on crafted debug info, producing wrong source lines.

title: Unchecked usize addition for proto end
description: `start + proto_size as usize` can overflow/panic with an attacker-controlled ULEB128 proto-size before the bounds check.

title: Negative jump target wraps to huge usize
description: `(pc as i32 + 1 + d_signed) as usize` produces a meaningless target address when the branch offset is negative.

title: KN double constant flag bit not cleared before shift
description: `(kval << 32) | lo` leaves the integer-flag LSB embedded in bit 32 of the reconstructed f64 bits, corrupting any KN float whose high u32 LSB is set.

title: Unchecked u32 add of first_line+line offset
description: `first_line as u32 + line` can silently wrap for crafted debug info, yielding wrong source-line numbers.

title: Unchecked usize add for proto end offset
description: `start + proto_size as usize` can overflow (debug panic / release wraparound) before the `end > data.len()` bounds check on a hostile ULEB128 size.

title: Fat header nfat read with wrong endianness
description: Apple fat headers are always stored big-endian on disk; when `big_endian` (i.e. magic==FAT_CIGAM after LE decode) the branch incorrectly uses `read_u32_le` for nfat instead of `read_u32_be`, so slice count is byte-swapped and parse_fat returns garbage on the only real fat layout.

title: read_cstr off+max_len can overflow usize
description: `let end = off + max_len;` is unchecked; an attacker-controlled load command supplying a large name_off can panic on 32-bit usize or wrap on release builds, causing incorrect slicing.

title: Symtab base index can overflow
description: `symoff as usize + i * entry_size` is unchecked multiplication/addition; with crafted nsyms (u32 up to ~4B) and entry_size 16 this overflows usize on 32-bit hosts and may also wrap, skipping the bounds check.

title: Lazy bind entries not flagged as lazy
description: The loop comments "mark lazy binds" but the body is `let _ = e;` — lazy binds are stored indistinguishably from regular binds, breaking downstream lazy-vs-eager classification.

title: All imports attributed to dylibs[0]
description: `build_imports` assigns every undefined external symbol's dylib to `dylibs.first()`, so for any TWOLEVEL binary with multiple dependencies (the norm) every import is mislabeled.

title: Unchecked left shift on attacker-controlled mini_sector_size_exp
description: `1usize << mini_sector_size_exp` panics in debug and is UB-shaped (wrap) in release when exponent â‰¥ usize::BITS, with no validation of the u16 read from the header.

title: sector_slice_raw offset multiplication can wrap
description: `CFB_HEADER_SIZE + id as usize * sector_size` is not checked_mul; a crafted sector id can wrap and pass the subsequent `offset + sector_size > data.len()` length check, returning the wrong slice.

title: FAT sector offset uses unchecked multiplication
description: `(sector_id as usize + 1) * sector_size` is computed before the bounds compare; with 4096-byte sectors a malicious DIFAT entry near u32::MAX overflows usize on 32-bit and bypasses the guard.

title: size_hi used unconditionally for v3 files
description: Per MS-CFB, size high 4 bytes must be ignored for version-3 files (where they may be non-zero/garbage); using `(size_hi<<32)|size_lo` inflates stream size, breaking downstream reads or triggering huge allocations.

title: mini_stream_start assumes dir_entries[0] is root
description: `dir_entries.first()` is used without checking `entry_type == 5`; if directory layout puts root elsewhere or first entry is empty, mini-stream reads use wrong start sector.

title: e_res2 read from wrong offset
description: The loop reads e_res2 starting at byte 36, overlapping e_oemid/e_oeminfo; per IMAGE_DOS_HEADER layout e_res2 begins at offset 40, so e_res2 and e_oemid/e_oeminfo are corrupted.

title: read_rva integer overflow on off+size
description: `file_data.get(off..off + size)` can panic via arithmetic overflow when off+size exceeds usize::MAX with attacker-controlled inputs; should use checked_add.

title: RVA mapping uses max(vsize,raw_size)
description: Using `virtual_size.max(size_of_raw_data)` to bound the section can map RVAs past the on-disk data to file offsets beyond the raw section, yielding bytes from an unrelated region.

title: try_into.unwrap_or hides truncated reads
description: The closure reads `data[off..off+2]`; if off+2 > data.len() this panics before reaching unwrap_or, making the defensive default misleading (true for r16/r32/r64 across all parsers).

title: LEB128 u32 5th-byte high bits silently truncated
description: `u32::from(b & 0x7F) << shift` accepts byte with value bits > 0x0F at shift=28, silently dropping high bits and producing a wrong u32 with no MalformedLeb128 error.

title: memory.grow scan treats immediates as opcodes
description: `check_memory_grow` walks every byte of code looking for 0x40, with no opcode/immediate decoding, so any LEB128 immediate byte equal to 0x40 produces a false memory.grow finding.

title: parse_global silently accepts unterminated init expr
description: If section ends without 0x0B end opcode the loop exits via `off < data.len()` with no error returned, producing a malformed global parsed as valid.

title: Invalid table elem type silently coerced to FuncRef
description: `decode_valtype(elem_type).unwrap_or(ValType::FuncRef)` swallows invalid encodings instead of erroring, masking malformed binaries.

title: Relocator silently wraps on overflow
description: `base.wrapping_add(addr)` discards overflow, so a too-large addr can wrap below `base` and produce a bogus relocated address with no diagnostic.

title: InitializeParams uses snake_case without camelCase rename
description: JSON-RPC `initialize` sends `protocolVersion`/`clientInfo` but the struct fields are `protocol_version`/`client_info` with no serde rename, so params parsing silently fails and client_info is never recorded.

title: initialize sets Ready even when params fail to parse
description: `state = SessionState::Ready` is unconditionally set after the `if let` block, so a malformed initialize still readies the session instead of erroring.

title: Holding proxy_handlers read lock across user handler call
description: `handlers.get(&specific_key)` keeps the RwLock read guard alive while invoking the user handler, which will deadlock if the handler calls `register_proxy_handler` (writer) on the same FederatedServer.

title: min_length cast u64->usize truncates on 32-bit
description: `optional_u64(...).unwrap_or(4) as usize` silently truncates large user-supplied values on 32-bit targets, defeating the filter.

title: max=0 silently yields zero xrefs without error
description: Passing `max: 0` to `get_xrefs` produces an empty list rather than rejecting the invalid bound, masking client bugs.

title: probe uses GET instead of MCP JSON-RPC POST
description: `probe_server_tools_sync` issues a plain HTTP GET, which is not the MCP `tools/list` protocol, so real servers will never be discovered.

title: exponential glob backtracking enables DoS
description: `glob_match_inner` recurses on every `*` branch with no memoization, so patterns from config like `****x` against long tool names cause exponential blowup.

title: parse_http_addr drops port for URLs with paths but no port
description: URLs like `http://host/rpc` produce host with no port, so TcpStream::connect fails for valid HTTP endpoints.

title: XrefsTool truncates 64-bit address to low 32 bits
description: `needle[..4]` only matches first 4 bytes of `addr.to_le_bytes()`, so high addresses collide and high bits are silently ignored producing false xrefs.

title: AnalyzeCfgTool gives wrong size for RET imm16 (0xC2)
description: 0xC2 is encoded as 3 bytes (RET imm16) but is treated as size 1, misaligning all downstream basic-block boundaries.

title: Conditional-jump detection only covers JZ/JNZ (0x74/0x75)
description: Short Jcc opcodes 0x70-0x7F all terminate blocks; missing the other 14 causes incorrect CFG for any other conditional branch.

title: HexDump offset/length u64-to-usize cast unchecked
description: Untrusted `offset`/`length` from JSON are cast `as usize`, truncating on 32-bit targets and producing wrong slices instead of returning an error.

title: LargeWindowProvider cache offset wraps on addr below base
description: wrapping_sub before the `addr.0 >= base.0` check produces a huge offset that still passes `offset + len <= cache.len()` only by coincidence and otherwise reads wrong data on a hit, plus `offset + len` itself can overflow usize.

title: LargeWindowProvider cache hit silently truncates read
description: on hit it returns `cache[offset..offset+len]` but on miss it returns only `len.min(window_data.len())` bytes, hiding short reads from callers expecting `len` bytes.

title: `addr + len as u64` overflows in read_from_snapshot
description: adding `len as u64` to `addr` without checked_add can wrap on near-u64::MAX addresses, then the overlap check and `copy_start - addr` subtraction misbehave.

title: `wrapping_add` masks end-address overflow in write
description: computing `end_addr` with wrapping_add lets a write of length that overflows the address space silently wrap to 0, then the loop terminates immediately and the bounds check never fires.

title: `end_addr()` can overflow
description: `self.base_addr + self.data.len() as u64` is an unchecked add that can wrap to a low address, producing an invalid `AddressRange` reported through `regions()`.

title: V2 USE_EXTRA branch always reads extras index 0
description: `start == SLIDE_V2_PAGE_USE_EXTRA` is an exact-equality check, so `start & !SLIDE_V2_PAGE_USE_EXTRA` is always 0 and the real extras index in the low bits is never used.

title: end_address can overflow on large counts
description: `target_address + count*skip` uses non-saturating u64 add despite saturating_mul, so a high target_address plus a non-overflowing product can still wrap to a smaller value.

title: hash mask assumes power-of-two capacity without check
description: `h & (self.capacity - 1)` produces wrong buckets when capacity is not a power of two and underflows if `capacity == 0` is bypassed elsewhere.

title: read_at_va can panic via off+len overflow
description: `lc.data.get(off..off + len)` does not use checked addition; a malicious `len` near `usize::MAX` makes `off+len` wrap and either panic or pass the slice check incorrectly.

title: chain ptr_off advance can wrap or escape page
description: `ptr_off += delta as usize * 4` is unchecked and lets a malformed delta walk past the page or overflow usize, only caught later by the `+8 > data.len()` test which doesn't bound to the page.

title: resolve uses signed-to-unsigned cast that wraps
description: `(header_offset as i64 + field_offset as i64) as usize` silently wraps for negative results instead of erroring, producing huge offsets that bypass intent of validation.

title: FAT magic read with wrong endianness
description: FAT Mach-O headers are big-endian on disk (0xCAFEBABE) but `u32_le` is used to read the magic, so real FAT binaries will never match FAT_MAGIC and FairPlay detection silently skips them.

title: FAT nfat_arch/offset/size read little-endian
description: nfat_arch and per-arch offset/size in the FAT header are big-endian; reading via `u32_le` yields byte-swapped values that produce wrong slice offsets and bogus per-arch parsing.

title: Shift overflow on attacker-controlled page_size
description: `1usize << self.code_directory.page_size` panics when `page_size >= 64` (parsed unchecked from input bytes), crashing `verify_hashes` on malformed signatures.

title: Unchecked `count * 8` in SuperBlob index
description: `12 + count * 8` (with count from a u32 read from input) can overflow usize on 32-bit targets, bypassing the truncation check and allowing OOB-style continue/decoding.

title: Unchecked `(i+1)*hash_sz` multiplication
description: For attacker-controlled n_special_slots and hash_size, `(i+1)*hash_sz` can overflow usize while iterating, producing wrong `start` offsets via `saturating_sub` and skewed special-hash extraction.

title: packed-switch payload size off-by-4
description: Returns `2 + sz*2` code units but the packed-switch payload header is 4 code units (ident, size, int first_key) so size should be `4 + sz*2`, causing PC advancement to land mid-payload and corrupt subsequent disassembly.

title: Fmt22x register truncated from 16-bit to 8-bit
description: `u8::try_from(word(1)).unwrap_or(u8::MAX)` clamps vBBBB (a real 16-bit register index per Dalvik spec) to 255, silently misidentifying registers >=256.

title: Fmt32x both 16-bit registers truncated to u8
description: `vaaaa & 0xff` and `vbbbb & 0xff` discard the upper byte of two full 16-bit register operands, producing wrong register names for any method using >256 registers.

title: Fmt3rc starting register truncated to u8
description: `cccc.wrapping_add(...) & 0xff` truncates a 16-bit base register CCCC plus 8-bit count, causing wrong register references for invoke/filled-new-array-range.

title: Fmt21h opcode discrimination wrong for long-hi
description: Only opcode `0x19` is shifted by 48; the const-wide/high16 path lacks distinction between 32-bit (`0x15`) and 64-bit forms via opcode rather than instr type, risking incorrect immediate width when reused.

title: Out-of-bounds slice in decode_invoke_35c-like
description: reg_count comes from high nibble (up to 15) and is used to slice a 5-element array, causing index-out-of-bounds panic on malformed bytecode.

title: Same OOB slice in decode_invoke_35c
description: reg_count can exceed 5 and is used as upper bound on a 5-element array, causing panic.

title: Empty/missing-paren signature panics
description: If signature has no '(' or is empty, `&sig[1..0]` panics due to start>end slice.

title: F11n sign-extension is wrong
description: `nibble_b.cast_signed() >> 4` operates on already-masked 4-bit value, producing 0/-1 instead of sign-extending the 4-bit literal.

title: F35c register count not clamped
description: `count` can be up to 15 and indexes a 6-element table via `i.min(5)`, silently duplicating reg_c for invalid encodings instead of erroring.

title: TcpSegment::to_bytes panics when data_offset < 5
description: `hl - 20` underflows usize when `data_offset` is 0â€“4, causing an immediate panic on attacker-controlled or default-modified segments.

title: PacketCraft::build never updates IPv4 total_length/checksum after stacking
description: `ip.to_bytes()` is called with the header's stale total_length (often 20), so emitted packets have wrong length and wrong checksum, making them invalid on the wire.

title: Ipv4Header::new can overflow total_length
description: `20 + payload_len` is a plain u16 add that wraps silently when payload_len > 65515, producing a tiny total_length that downstream parsers will accept while skipping data.

title: TCP data_offset field silently truncated
description: `self.data_offset << 4` on a u8 discards bits when data_offset > 15, so a caller setting data_offset=16 produces a header advertising offset 0 instead of erroring.

title: UdpDatagram::new silently caps length at u16::MAX
description: `saturating_add`+`unwrap_or(u16::MAX)` quietly accepts oversized payloads and emits a UDP header whose length field disagrees with the actual datagram, corrupting parsing on the receiver.

title: HashMap eviction picks arbitrary stream, not oldest
description: `streams.keys().next()` on a HashMap returns an unordered key, so the "evict oldest" path drops a random active stream instead of the LRU one.

title: HTTP PDU extractor silently mis-splits responses without Content-Length
description: When Content-Length is missing (e.g. chunked or HTTP/1.0 close-delimited), body_len defaults to 0 and the body bytes are reinterpreted as the next HTTP request, corrupting PDU boundaries.

title: GapDetector merge ignores TCP sequence-number wraparound
description: Ranges are compared with raw `u32` ordering and `s <= last.1`, so a segment whose seq wraps past 2^32 is sorted incorrectly and never merged with the pre-wrap range.

title: TimeSeriesData.record only checks the last bucket
description: An out-of-order timestamp produces a new bucket appended after a later one, breaking monotonic ordering and creating duplicate buckets for the same bucket_ts.

title: current_bps over-counts by including the first sample in the numerator
description: `total_bytes` sums every sample but the time span is `last_ts - first_ts`, so the first sample's bytes are attributed to a zero-length interval and inflate the bps result.

title: LenLt(0) subtracts 1 from u32 zero
description: `*n - 1` panics in debug / wraps to u32::MAX in release when filter `LenLt(0)` is compiled.

title: parse_pcapng_block underflows on block_len<4
description: `off + block_len - 4` subtracts from usize without bounds check; a crafted block_len of 0..3 panics or wraps the index.

title: BPF LenGt/LenLt never uses packet length
description: `LD_IMM` loads the immediate `u32::MAX` into A instead of the packet length, so the length comparisons are constant and the filter is broken.

title: BPF And/Or just concatenates programs
description: First sub-program always ends in RET which exits the VM, making the second sub-program dead code; And/Or/Not compositions produce wrong accept/reject results.

title: StreamBuffer.insert drops new data on duplicate seq
description: `or_insert_with` keeps the existing (possibly shorter) segment and silently discards the new payload at the same seq, causing data loss when a retransmission carries more bytes.

title: AhoCorasick state count truncates silently
description: goto.len as u32 truncates instead of panicking.

title: Depth/Within/Distance usize addition can panic
description: current_offset + d can overflow usize.

title: PCRE check silently skipped on non-UTF8 payload
description: from_utf8 unwrap_or empty string causes fail-open/closed.

title: overlay end computed without bounding by raw_size
description: `has_overlay` computes `raw_off + raw_size` as `usize` without checking for wrapping; a corrupt/hostile PE with large raw_size causes integer wrap, producing a false-negative overlay result.

title: manifest detection false-positive via byte scan
description: `has_manifest` matches the 4-byte pattern anywhere in file data, not only in the resource directory, causing false positives on arbitrary file content that happens to contain those bytes.

title: wide-string case comparison on UTF-16 bytes is incorrect
description: `has_resource_type` calls `eq_ignore_ascii_case` on the raw UTF-16LE bytes of the lowercased needle, which are not ASCII and so the comparison is byte-exact, defeating the stated case-insensitive purpose.

title: entry-point section range uses virt_size.max(1) not raw_size
description: `get_entry_point_bytes` uses `virt_size.max(1)` as the upper bound for EP-RVA containment, so a section with virt_size=0 always includes the EP, yielding a wrong file offset and corrupted EP bytes.

title: confidence formula ignores per-signature weight
description: `build_detection` sets confidence as `sigs.len() * 0.3` capped at 1.0, so a single weak signature and three strong signatures both yield identical confidence values, making the score meaningless.

title: block offset u64 truncation in analyze_blocks
description: `(i * block_size) as u64` performs the multiplication in `usize` before casting, silently wrapping on 32-bit targets when `i * block_size` overflows usize.

title: same usize-overflow in BlockHeatmap::build
description: `(i * block_size) as u64` multiplies in usize first, truncating silently on 32-bit targets for large files.

title: e_lfanew read uses wrong field offsets
description: COFF optional-header size is read from `pe_data[e_lfanew + 20..22]` but the field at PE+20 is SizeOfOptionalHeader only when the 4-byte PE sig and 20-byte COFF header are correct; code also reads `num_sections` from `pe_data[e_lfanew + 6]` instead of `e_lfanew + 4 + 6`, missing the 4-byte PE signature offset.

title: Welford stddev update stores RMS not stddev
description: `update()` stores `sqrt(running_sum_of_squares / n)` in the `stddev` field; the running value is the root-mean-square deviation, not the sample standard deviation, producing wrong z-scores.

title: running average of merged block entropy is wrong
description: When adjacent high-entropy blocks are merged, `last.entropy = (last.entropy + e) / 2.0` gives a simple two-point average regardless of how many blocks have already been merged, progressively underweighting earlier blocks.

title: import count heuristic double-counts overlapping .dll/.DLL
description: `count_nonoverlapping` is called twice with case variants on the same byte range; a mixed-case string like .Dll is counted by neither, giving inconsistent proxy import counts.

title: Rich search panics on short e_lfanew
description: `pe_data[0x80..search_end]` panics when `e_lfanew < 0x80` because `search_end < 0x80` produces an invalid slice range.

title: u32 wrapping in section RVA comparison
description: `va + vs` can wrap on u32 for a crafted PE, causing the EP-in-section check to give wrong results.

title: opt_off+20 not bounds-checked before EP RVA read
description: `data[opt_off+16..19]` is accessed after only checking `pe_off+24 <= len`, not `opt_off+20 <= len`.

title: full-file scan only checks at offset 0
description: Non-EP signatures are matched with `sig.matches_at(data, 0)` only, so they never slide across the file and miss all non-zero occurrences.

title: `search_end.min(pe_data.len())` still allows 0x80 panic
description: `e_lfanew` can be smaller than 0x80, making `pe_data[0x80..search_end]` an inverted/empty range that panics.

title: EmptyDatabase error for valid file with empty patterns
description: If all parsed entries had empty patterns (silently dropped), `parse_userdb` returns `Err(EmptyDatabase)` even on a well-formed file, conflating parse success with content policy.

title: MatchOffset preview uses entire data slice instead of match bytes
description: `MatchOffset::new` receives `data` as the slice starting at the match, but `length` is set to `data.len()` (the whole remaining slice length) rather than the actual matched-region length, so `length` is always wrong.

title: step_back returns wrong position
description: After decrementing event_index, it reads events[event_index - 1].position (the event before the new index), but it should read events[event_index].position to reflect the event the cursor now points at.

title: Watchpoint overlap check can overflow
description: `access_addr + access_len` and `self.address + self.size` are unchecked u64 additions that wrap on extremely large values, potentially making non-overlapping regions appear to overlap.

title: TtdSequenceId::from(TracePosition) silently truncates step
description: TracePosition::step is u64 but TtdSequenceId::minor is u32; the cast `p.step as u32` silently drops the upper 32 bits, corrupting positions with step > u32::MAX.

title: decode_events silently drops trailing data on unknown tag
description: When an unrecognized tag byte is encountered the loop breaks without returning an error, silently discarding all remaining events instead of reporting a corrupt-data error.

title: TtdModuleList::read allocates up to 4096 entries without validating count against stream
description: count is capped at 4096 for Vec::with_capacity but the loop still iterates count times, so a malicious file with count > 4096 causes unbounded heap allocation.

title: DataFlow query never matches anything
description: The filter checks that a write-to-source position is also in `writes_to_sink` - two disjoint addresses can never share the same TracePosition, so the result is always empty.

title: Heap alloc/free classification by index parity
description: `detect_heap_operations` classifies calls as alloc vs free using `idx.is_multiple_of(2)` (event array index parity), which is semantically meaningless and produces incorrect results for any real trace.

title: CallChain ignores ordering - reports false positives
description: `eval_query(CallChain)` checks only that any `Call { to }` exists anywhere in the trace, then returns all `Call { from }` events regardless of whether they precede that call, making the chain check vacuous.

title: `as u64` cast on `elapsed().as_millis()` silently truncates
description: `as_millis()` returns `u128`; casting to `u64` silently wraps for traces longer than ~585 million years, but for very long traces this truncates without any check or error.

title: Sequence matcher never resets on mismatch - skips overlapping matches
description: When an event does not match `patterns[pat_idx]` the pattern index is not reset to 0, so the automaton stalls mid-sequence and misses all subsequent potential matches.

title: Syscall number silently truncated from u64 to u32
description: `parse_hex_or_dec` returns `u64`; it is cast to `u32` with `as u32`, silently discarding the high 32 bits if a large value is supplied.

title: And-plan always joins qs[0] with qs[1] even for >2 sub-queries
description: `plan_node(And)` selects `qs[1.min(qs.len()-1)]` as the right child, meaning a single-element And joins the only element with itself, and all elements beyond index 1 are ignored in the plan.

title: fetch_update closure stores pre-increment value
description: `c.checked_add(1).map(|_| c)` stores the old value `c` back (not `c+1`), so the counter never advances and every encrypt call uses counter=0, reusing nonces.

title: u128 nanoseconds cast silently truncates high bits
description: `(n >> 64) as u64` shifts a `u128` right by 64 then truncates to u64; the top-64-bit XOR contribution is correct but `n as u64` silently discards the upper 64 bits without the comment acknowledging this as intentional folding.

title: `memory_events` metric uses integer division losing remainder
description: `n / 5 * 2` loses up to 4 events due to integer truncation before multiplication (e.g. n=63 gives 24 instead of 25).

title: output path constructed from unvalidated `output_dir` string
description: `Path::new(&self.config.output_dir).join(...)` never sanitizes `output_dir`, so a caller-supplied `../../../etc` traverses outside the intended directory.

title: `payload.len() as u32` silently wraps for payloads > 4 GiB
description: `TraceChunk::new` stores `payload.len() as u32` with no overflow check; a large payload records a wrong `uncompressed_size` in the chunk header without error.

title: `notify_event` always passes `tid=0` to `should_record`
description: Thread-ID is hardcoded to `0u32` instead of using the `tid` argument - thread-based filters are silently bypassed for all events.

title: run_forward_to_position rejects valid forward seek
description: Returns PositionNotFound when target_idx == event_index (i.e. the current event), so seeking to the already-current position fails silently instead of being a no-op.

title: metadata length silently truncated to u32
description: `meta_bytes.len() as u32` truncates without a bounds check; a metadata blob >4 GiB writes a wrong length prefix, corrupting the stream and any subsequent reader.
